articles.title: Canada opens bank stablecoin access, but strips deposit guarantees
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Canada proposes requiring bank groups that issue stablecoins to use non-financial subsidiaries regulated under the Stablecoin Act.
- The budget would also extend the framework to foreign financial institutions outside Canadian prudential supervision.
- Covered tokens would not be publicly deposit insured, and the proposed changes still require legislation.
Canada's Nov. 5 budget proposes requiring banks and other federally regulated financial institutions that issue stablecoins to do so through separate subsidiaries, bringing those issuers under the Stablecoin Act alongside nonbank issuers.
The proposed subsidiaries would be non-financial institutions regulated under the Act. Budget 2026 also proposes extending the framework to foreign financial institutions that are not prudentially regulated in Canada, with consistent treatment across issuers as its stated goal.
A stablecoin issued by a bank-owned company would still fall within a framework that separates covered tokens from publicly insured deposits.
The legislative annex proposes amending the Bank Act, Trust and Loan Companies Act, and Insurance Companies Act to prohibit federally regulated financial institutions from issuing stablecoins directly.
The existing Stablecoin Act excludes financial-institution issuers, subject to regulations. Routing issuance through a non-financial-institution subsidiary would bring that issuing entity within the stablecoin framework.
The Bank of Canada says its role under the Act will include registering non-financial institution issuers, supervising compliance, monitoring issuance and redemption risks, and taking enforcement action.
The planned foreign-institution extension targets institutions outside Canadian prudential supervision. The annex also proposes clarifying that stablecoin issuance is not deposit-taking for foreign banks and their affiliates covered by Part XII of the Bank Act.
The existing Act separately excludes central banks, and also lets the Bank of Canada Governor grant conditional exemptions where provincial or foreign rules are substantially similar.
What holders would receive
Once applicable, the Act's safeguards would require redemption at face value in the currency a stablecoin tracks.
It would also require reserves worth at least the outstanding face value, and qualified custody that segregates reserve assets and protects them from issuer and custodian creditor claims other than holders' redemption claims. Those duties remain subject to the Act's statutory and regulatory terms.
Sections 33 and 34 would prohibit covered stablecoins from being deposits, publicly deposit-insured instruments or government-guaranteed or backstopped instruments, and prohibit representations suggesting those features.
A bank parent's involvement would not convert the token into an insured savings balance.
The budget also promises continued engagement on stronger consumer protections if an issuer or custodian becomes insolvent.
The Act received royal assent on March 26, but its operating provisions take effect on dates set by order of the Governor in Council.
The Oct. 24 proposed-regulations impact statement identifies fall 2027 as the intended commencement window for the wider framework.
The budget's new development concerns who would issue within the framework, while implementation still depends on legislation and commencement.

articles.title: EU Taps Industry to Set Standards for Tokenized Securities
articles.text:
EU taps industry to set standards for tokenized securities
Applications close Nov. 27 for an industry group that aims to draft initial standards for holding and settling tokenized securities by early 2028.
The European Central Bank, European Commission and European Securities and Markets Authority are seeking nominations for an industry-led group that will draft common standards for holding and settling tokenized securities.
Eligible applicants include EU industry associations, global institutions, private firms and fintech companies. They can apply to the European Tokenisation Standards Group (ETSG) by Nov. 27, with work set to begin in January 2027, according to a release published Monday. The three EU institutions will participate as observers.
The group will develop technical and market standards to help companies hold and settle tokenized securities across different distributed ledger technology (DLT) platforms and ensure those platforms can work with existing financial systems. The group aims to produce an initial set of standards by early 2028, according to its mandate. The standards will support Appia, the Eurosystem’s initiative to develop a blueprint for Europe’s tokenized financial markets.
The institutions warned that fragmentation could limit the benefits of tokenization and said the group may recommend ways for EU authorities to encourage firms to adopt its standards.
In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that allows financial institutions to settle wholesale transactions in tokenized assets in central bank money.
Related: ECB President Christine Lagarde to step down in February 2027

articles.title: Solana Set for Another Tokenized Stock Venue as Formation Notifies the SEC - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Formation Securities notified the SEC it intends to run a tokenized securities venue on Solana under the agency’s “Innovation Exemption,” with trading expected in early 2027.
- The venue promises 24/7 trading and near-instant atomic settlement while preserving shareholders’ voting and dividend rights.
- It joins a crowded onchain-stock race from the NYSE-Avalanche deal to the OKX-ICE venue—and builds on the Solana-backed Project Open proposal.
A new firm is lining up to become one of the first to trade tokenized U.S. stocks onchain, notifying the Securities and Exchange Commission that it intends to run a tokenized securities venue on Solana.
Formation Securities said Monday it had filed the notice to operate under the SEC’s “Innovation Exemption,” the conditional relief the agency issued in September that lets eligible tokenized stocks trade through permissioned automated market maker pools on qualifying venues.
Trading is expected to begin in early 2027, with tokenized shares of Exodus Movement, Forward Industries and Galaxy Digital anticipated at launch.
SOL next move: Pump to $160 or Dump to $40?
The pitch is to deliver the benefits of blockchain trading, 24/7 markets and near-instant settlement, without stripping away the rights investors expect from real stock.
Under the exemption, eligible tokens must carry the same voting and dividend rights as traditional shares, and each trade settles atomically onchain, a feature meant to cut settlement risk. A company’s transfer agent still keeps the official shareholder record, while every trade posts to the public ledger in real time.
“Tokenized stocks will succeed only if public companies see the value in them, and we intend to build this market together with issuers,” said Christopher Montagano, president of Formation Securities, which licenses its trading technology from Solana-based exchange Orca.
Tokenization firms Securitize and Superstate are expected to supply tokenized shares, with Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo noting its tokens are each backed by a real share held by its broker-dealer.
Access will be limited to verified investors, who can reach the venue through Formation’s platform and distributors including Alpaca, CoinList’s Passage, custodians Anchorage, BitGo and Fireblocks, and wallet providers Solflare and Squads.
The move adds another entrant to a fast-crowding race to put stocks onchain. The NYSE recently tapped Solana rival Avalanche to settle its own planned tokenized securities platform, Securitize launched tokenized stocks on Solana, and an OKX-ICE venue is also in the works, though every Magnificent Seven stock opted out of that one.
The effort builds on Project Open, a proposal a coalition including Orca, Superstate and the Solana Policy Institute submitted to the SEC in 2025.
Formation chose Solana, it said, for its speed, low costs and track record with tokenized assets, noting the network hosts more than $5 billion in tokenized real-world assets.

articles.title: Vitalik Buterin Moves On From ‘Ultrasound Money,’ Says ETH’s Value Is Stability - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin argued ETH should be valued as a store of value rather than a fee-burning token, saying the burn was “never a true floor.”
- Ethlabs’ Binji Pande told Decrypt that ETH is a more “future-proof store of value” than Bitcoin, citing quantum and AI threats.
- It marks a notable shift in messaging from the Ethereum community, after ETH was branded as "ultrasound money" in 2021.
Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin wants people to stop valuing ETH as a fee-burning token and start treating it as a store of value, arguing that the burn was "never" as strong as it seemed. Binji Pande, founding member of Ethlabs, told Decrypt that he agrees, claiming that it is a more "future-proof store of value" than Bitcoin.
It's a notable shift in messaging from the Ethereum community, after ETH was branded as "ultrasound money" when the network started burning a portion of every transaction fee in 2021. The argument was that as more people used Ethereum, fewer coins would exist in circulation, and fewer coins meant a higher price. Now, however, Buterin claims that isn't as important as people may think.
"We should not feel sad if fee burn is < 10% of breakeven indefinitely; the value of ETH comes from elsewhere," Buterin tweeted on Sunday. That value, he argued, is stability, which comes from Ethereum being decentralized, resistant to censorship, and having strong security.
Expanding on why I believe "ETH as store of value (SoV)" makes much more sense to focus on than "ETH as fee-burning token".
Three primary reasons:
1. ETH as fee-burning token never was as strong as it seemed
2. Optimizing for ETH as fee-burning token would demand Ethereum and…
— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) November 8, 2026
Those in favour of the fee-burning structure argued that fees gave ETH a price floor, much like a company's stock may be backed by revenue and profits. From 2021 to 2023, Ethereum burned millions of ETH every year, but Buterin said this was "never a true floor." Most of these burns, he said, came from internal crypto uses like lending and silly NFT purchases.
Connor Howe, co-founder and CEO of infrastructure provider Enso, told Decrypt that Ethereum's layer-2 expansion made the fee-burning argument worse. Connor said that a significant portion of activity has moved onto layer-2s, and users pay "almost nothing" to settle transactions. To optimize a fee-burning token, he added, you'd also want to optimise for higher gas prices—which no one wants.
"If we decide we actually want to optimize ETH for burning fees to justify a present-day ~$270B market cap, then Ethereum would essentially be functioning as a world-scale major corporation," Buterin said. In doing that, Ethereum would lose one of its major selling points: decentralization.
"I agree with Vitalik, and I also believe that ETH is best positioned as a future-proof store of value," Ethlabs' Pande told Decrypt. He highlighted that the network is censorship-resistant, that it has "great distribution," is widely available, and that it is "at the center of future growing sectors such as tokenization, Stablecoins, and DeFi."
Store of value
A store of value is an asset that holds its worth over time, meaning investors can put their money into it without fearing it will disappear. Historically, gold has been seen as the ultimate store of value, and Bitcoin supporters have pitched it as a "digital gold."
Pande, however, argues that both fall short compared to Ethereum.
"Gold has held the SoV role for a long time, but given the world we live in now is much more globalized, we need increased portability, something gold simply cannot offer," Pande told Decrypt. "Storing gold is simply not useful either past a certain point; you reach physical limits."
When it comes to Bitcoin as a store of value, Pande expressed concern that it isn't "future-proof" as AI and quantum threats loom.
Ethereum has been preparing for those threats for a while. In January, the Ethereum Foundation formed a dedicated post-quantum team and, more recently, researchers have debated the potential AI-powered threats. By contrast, the Bitcoin community appears more fractured on how to tackle the quantum threat.
"Security is ingrained more deeply into Ethereum’s culture than anywhere else," Julian Ma, co-founder of Ethlabs, told Decrypt. "AI being used for cyberattacks and potentially breaking cryptography strengthens ETH's position as a programmable store-of-value asset because the years of preparation and large investments into security and formal verification of the Ethereum protocol and its applications are about to pay off."
Pande added that newer assets can’t compete with ETH as a store of value, because there’s no way to verify they’re fairly distributed. The Ethereum Foundation owns less than 0.2% of ETH, he said, and the token has traded for 11 years.
ETH price on November 10, 4:59PM UTC
“Trying to distribute or mine a new asset as a SoV in the lord’s 2026 is like trying to hide a sack of meat in a sea of piranhas,” he said. “It can and WILL get centralized.”
Not everyone thinks Ethereum’s leadership got here quickly enough, though. Howe said the Ethereum Foundation “needs to start to actually listen and look at the applications building on top of their network.”
“I think he is right,” Howe said of Buterin's recent tweet, “and I think it took too long to say it.”

articles.title: Coinbase Receives OCC Approval for National Trust Bank Charter
articles.text:
Coinbase’s US national trust bank charter takes effect
Coinbase plans to expand its institutional crypto custody business under the federal charter and is exploring digital asset payment products.
Coinbase’s national trust bank charter took effect on Friday, according to the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC).
The applied for the charter in October 2025 and received preliminary approval in April 2026, according to the OCC’s filing record. The charter allows Coinbase National Trust Company to hold digital assets on behalf of clients as a fiduciary, according to the OCC’s preliminary approval letter.
Coinbase plans to offer institutional clients segregated custody accounts, with access to staking, financing and trading through other Coinbase entities, according to its charter application.
Coinbase’s application also outlined plans to explore digital asset payment products and custody services that would allow clients to interact with select smart contracts.
Other crypto companies that received OCC national trust bank charters include Ripple, Circle, BitGo, Fidelity Digital Assets and Paxos.
Crypto.com and Stripe-owned Bridge received conditional approval, while Kraken and EDX Markets are still pursuing charters.
Related: Hyperliquid Strategies seeks futures registration for perps

articles.title: Amundi puts European stocks on Ethereum, but access terms stay hidden
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Amundi announced a tokenized Core STOXX Europe 600 share class on Nov. 5, issued on public Ethereum with CACEIS.
- The tokens represent investment fund units, giving exposure through the fund rather than direct shares in each underlying company.
- Amundi's announcement leaves eligibility, transfer and redemption terms unspecified, so Ethereum issuance alone does not establish unrestricted access.
Amundi has issued a tokenized share class of its Amundi Core STOXX Europe 600 equity index fund on public Ethereum on Nov. 5, adding a blockchain route to European stock-market exposure with CACEIS providing the technology and infrastructure for tokenizing the fund units
Amundi said the new class remains integrated into the fund's existing operating model, and investors can also continue accessing the fund through traditional channels.
The token represents a unit in an investment fund, with investors gaining exposure through that fund.
Amundi's model differs from those of companies objecting to third-party stock tokens on OKXICE and distinguishes those products from stock perpetual contracts that provide price exposure without share ownership.
Issuance on Ethereum doesn't guarantee access
The announcement does not specify eligible investors, minimum subscriptions, fees, transfer restrictions, or redemption procedures for the tokenized class.
Those details are key to anyone assessing whether they can buy, move, or redeem the units, since issuance on a public blockchain =does not establish unrestricted retail access or permissionless use across DeFi platforms.
CACEIS's October 2024 description of its general tokenization platform outlined a hybrid model combining traditional ownership records with blockchain units and digital investor checks, providing infrastructure context.
The equity class also extends Amundi's earlier work in cash management. Their EURXT settlement concerned a subscription into a tokenized Amundi money-market fund, and the firm's latest release likewise refers to earlier money-market and stablecoin initiatives.
The issuance establishes a fund-unit route onto Ethereum, with practical access dependent on the new class's terms.

articles.title: Tom Lee’s Bitmine Adds $20M in Ethereum, Seizing on Vitalik’s 'ETH Is Money' Declaration - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Bitmine bought another 9,587 ETH, raising holdings to 6,070,092 ETH (about $13.6 billion), or 4.97% of supply—99% of the way to its “Alchemy of 5%” goal.
- Chairman Tom Lee seized on Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin’s declaration that “ETH is a store of value, ETH is money,” calling it a “seismic shift."
- Total holdings hit $14.3 billion; Bitmine remains the top ETH treasury and No. 2 behind Strategy.
Bitmine Immersion Technologies extended its weekly Ethereum buying streak, adding 9,587 ETH worth roughly $20 million, as chairman Tom Lee pointed to a recent declaration by Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin as validation of the firm’s accumulation strategy.
The NYSE-listed company said Monday its holdings reached 6,070,092 ETH, worth roughly $13.6 billion at a reference price of $2,234 per coin.
That’s 4.97% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine, by its own count, 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, a target it calls the “Alchemy of 5%,” reached in just 15 months.
Ethereum next move: Pump to $3K or Dump to $1.5K?
The firm has bought Ethereum every week since launching its treasury strategy on June 30, 2025.
Lee leaned heavily on comments Buterin made at the Devcon conference in Mumbai, where the Ethereum founder said, “I’ve finally made up my mind, ETH is a store of value, ETH is money.” Lee called the declaration “a seismic shift,” arguing it clarifies how ETH will capture value in what he described as a coming “supercycle of tokenization and AI.” (Disclosure: Tom Lee is one of several investors in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent company.)
He contended ETH functions as “pristine and trusted collateral” rather than a cash-flow token, reflecting its position as the layer-1 network favored by financial institutions moving assets onchain.
Buterin elaborated in an X post, laying out why he now sees ETH primarily as a store of value, including his view that fee-burning is weaker than it once seemed and that optimizing for it can conflict with decentralization. Lee framed that reasoning as consistent with Ethereum’s roadmap and its role in the tokenization wave.
Counting cash, other tokens and “moonshot” investments, Bitmine’s total holdings stood at $14.3 billion as of Nov. 8, including 216 Bitcoin, $475 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and a $75 million position in Eightco Holdings, which it bills as a rare public proxy for indirect OpenAI exposure.
Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, trailing only Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which the release said holds about 849,327 BTC. Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, roughly 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized staking revenue of about $359 million.
The firm also recently argued the muted market reaction to the record Binance hack showed crypto’s growing resilience.

articles.title: Leios scaling threatens Cardano stability unless fast path passes
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Kevin Hammond proposed emergency exceptions for disabling Leios, while restarting would retain normal notice and frequency rules.
- CAP-12’s current draft forbids the zero setting, and Hammond’s proposed route requires switching tests across node implementations.
- Emergency deactivation would still require governance approval and epoch-boundary enactment.
Cardano could give governance a faster way to disable its proposed Leios scaling system during a serious network problem while keeping restarts under normal approval rules.
A Nov. 6 proposal from Kevin Hammond would relax notice and frequency limits for emergency deactivation, without removing the votes or enactment steps needed to change the protocol.
Hammond set out the approach in the Cardano Amendment Proposal 12 (CAP-12) technical discussion, calling it a proposed Technical Steering Committee position ahead of a Nov. 18 review. CAP-12 is a proposed constitutional amendment setting limits for Dijkstra-era protocol parameters.
CAP-12 version 5, which remained open on Nov. 8, prohibits zero-valued Leios parameters, and Hammond’s network-wide shutdown route would use one.
Cardano keeps ordinary restart
The proposed switch is intended to disable Leios’s additional transaction-processing path while preserving ordinary block production. It would set maxEndorserBlockTxsSize, the limit on transaction payload endorsed by a supplementary block, to zero.
These endorser blocks reference additional transactions, which enter the chain after certification and inclusion of the certificate in a later ranking block.
For a Severity 1 or Severity 2 network issue, Hammond’s fast path would waive the PARAM-04a notice requirement and permit the transition to zero in any epoch.
Switching Leios back on would follow the normal process and remain subject to the network-group frequency limit.
Hammond said ratification and enactment would still take at least one epoch boundary, describing a boundary the action must pass.
CAP-12’s analysis says Leios parameter changes require delegated representatives, the Constitutional Committee and a stake-pool-operator vote. Hammond separately distinguished that governance-controlled protocol switch from an operational switch based on ad-hoc operator participation.
Hammond made the protocol route conditional on written confirmation from the Linear Leios team about what zero does. No endorser blocks should be announced, no votes cast or diffused, and no certificates included in ranking blocks.
Node behavior should be equivalent to Praos, Cardano’s existing block-production system.
He also required switch-off and switch-back-on exercises on the Preview and Preprod test networks, with block production measured against the Praos baseline, plus conformance tests for the zero setting across all node implementations.
Constitutional permission to set a value would still need a matching implementation: clients must interpret zero consistently, and switching back on must work as intended.
Meanwhile, version 5’s MEBTS-09 rule expressly says the parameter must not be zero. Intersect’s Nov. 6 update confirms that the off switch was removed from the constitutional text, with deactivation left to the hard-fork plan and another draft expected.
Adopting Hammond’s route would require reconciling that ban with the proposed exception.
Testing and the constitutional timetable
The Nov. 3 working-group minutes say the test network entered the Dijkstra era on Nov. 2 using node 11.2, without full Leios implementation.
Intersect said on Nov. 6 that DijkstraNet supported BLS key registration but not full Linear Leios. Full Leios was available for early integration testing on Musashi, while the combined node 11.3 release candidate was estimated to be at least two to three weeks away.
The Nov. 3 consensus update reports endorser-block forging, certificate checks, and vote relaying. Essential Cardano’s Nov. 6 summary describes those main-branch changes as development work rather than a mainnet release.
The working-group minutes record an aim to submit the constitution and guardrails by Nov. 25.
Hammond also said on Nov. 6 that the Parameter Committee had not yet seen the pending numerical values and would need time to review them.

articles.title: Robinhood Launches US IPO Access for UK Retail Investors
articles.text:
Robinhood opens access to US IPOs for UK retail investors
Robinhood’s UK customers can request shares in eligible US initial public offerings at the offer price before the stocks begin trading.
Robinhood has launched a service that lets UK retail investors request shares in eligible US initial public offerings (IPOs) before trading begins.
Customers can use their existing investment accounts to review offering documents in the app and request shares at the IPO price without paying trading commissions, Robinhood said Monday.
Robinhood said it has participated in more than 50 IPOs since launching the service in the US in 2021. The company did not identify which upcoming US IPOs would be available to UK investors.

The expansion follows Robinhood’s third-quarter earnings report in October, when the company reported record revenue of $1.42 billion and net income of $476 million.

articles.title: XRP’s new euro cash-out route had less than €100 in its direct market
articles.text:
Quick Take
- GateHub announced EURGH redemption via SEPA, while XRP holders still need a separate conversion into the euro token.
- A Nov. 8 snapshot showed one funded direct-book offer of 96.80 EURGH in exchange for 484 XRP.
- The measured direct book covers one dated public market, not every GateHub bank-transfer or conversion route.
XRP holders seeking euros through GateHub's newly announced EURGH route faced just 96.80 euro tokens in the direct XRP/EURGH order book at a Nov. 8 ledger snapshot.
Wallet platform GateHub announced EURGH with Dinaro, the token's electronic-money issuer, on Nov. 5, saying its euro token on the XRP Ledger and Xahau could be redeemed through SEPA bank payments, subject to legal and verification requirements. For someone starting with XRP, however, obtaining that euro token comes before redeeming it. The measured public market offered little capacity for that first step.
A funded offer, at a steep price
At the validated XRPL ledger that closed Nov. 8 at 13:29:31 UTC, the direct order book returned one offer supplying 96.80 EURGH in exchange for 484 XRP. Its owner's available funds covered the token amount.
That works out to 0.20 EURGH per XRP before additional costs. Even treating each EURGH as one euro, as the issuer's stated redemption terms envisage, the entire displayed token inventory was worth less than €100.
The price was also far from the separate euro market. Kraken's XRP/EUR ticker, captured at 13:27:50 UTC, showed a best bid of €1.04544 per XRP. The observations were 101 seconds apart and covered different venues, before trading, transfer, redemption or banking costs. They were indicative quotes, not a guaranteed cash-out comparison. XRP's broader market was near $1.17 and down 6.70% over seven days in the Nov. 8 afternoon snapshot.
Still, the difference illustrates why a bank connection alone does not establish a competitive exit for XRP. The direct offer asked a seller to accept 0.20 EURGH for each XRP while a separate euro venue displayed a much higher bid. A token's redemption value and the exchange price available to acquire it are separate matters.
The issuer's outstanding XRPL obligations totaled 55,370.62 EURGH at the same ledger. That balance measures issued tokens, not XRP-buying liquidity. Xahau balances are outside this XRPL reading.
There was also no XRP/EURGH automated market maker pool at that ledger. Such a pool would be another place to look for conversion liquidity alongside the direct offers.
A request to convert XRP into 1,000 EURGH returned no route for the tested accounts. The sending account had sufficient XRP, and the receiving account already had room to hold more EURGH on its trust line, the ledger relationship needed to hold that issuer's token.
This was an account-specific routing result, not proof that every possible conversion was unavailable. XRPL's pathfinding documentation cautions that results are not guaranteed to find the best route. The resting offer also describes available terms, rather than a completed trade.
Hosted execution needs its own quote. GateHub's Exchange documentation describes market-based rates and immediate execution or cancellation; its Trade guide says Exchange calculates from current market orders. Those interfaces do not, by themselves, demonstrate a separate reserve of EURGH liquidity or a larger executable quote.
GateHub's Xaman on/off-ramp support also describes SEPA and SWIFT connectivity, with a verified GateHub account required. The measured EURGH constraint therefore cannot be extended to all GateHub bank-transfer channels.
Bank access and XRP holdings are different questions
GateHub says users can deposit euros by bank transfer and receive EURGH in their selected wallet. Dinaro is the issuer behind that token; GateHub describes its redemption into SEPA payments, subject to legal and verification requirements. Dinaro appears in Banka Slovenije's electronic-money institution register; that institutional entry does not separately identify EURGH.
The announced deposit flow does not itself require a large XRP trading position. XRP remains relevant for account reserves and transaction fees, while traders may choose to hold it as conversion inventory.
XRPL's auto-bridging mechanism can route between two issued tokens through XRP when suitable offers improve the exchange rate. It cannot create the missing inventory, and its existence does not demonstrate lasting demand to hold XRP.
For this euro route to become a more useful exit for XRP holders, the next evidence would be competitive funded quotes, successful larger conversions and attributable production usage. The Nov. 8 public snapshot exposed the conversion hurdle; GateHub's banking announcement addresses the redemption step after it.

articles.title: NYSE Taps Avalanche to Settle Its Planned Tokenized Stock Platform - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Ava Labs said Avalanche will provide the “core ledger technology” for the clearing firm behind an NYSE-affiliated tokenized securities platform, designed for 24/7 trading, clearing and settlement pending regulatory approval.
- The move is notable for putting a blockchain beneath the clearing-and-settlement layer—the market’s core plumbing—rather than just tokenizing an individual fund or stock.
- It adds to a Wall Street tokenization, from the NYSE-Blockchain.com deal to the OKX-ICE venue, which every Magnificent Seven stock opt
The New York Stock Exchange is turning to Avalanche to power the behind-the-scenes plumbing of its forthcoming tokenized securities platform, one of the clearest signs yet that Wall Street’s oldest institutions are moving core market infrastructure onto public blockchains.
Ava Labs, the company behind Avalanche, said Monday that the blockchain will serve as the “core ledger technology” for the clearing firm behind an NYSE-affiliated digital trading venue.
The platform, which the NYSE’s parent Intercontinental Exchange previously said it was developing, is designed to allow 24/7 trading, clearing and settlement of tokenized securities, subject to regulatory approval. Running on Avalanche, it aims to bring the clearing of tokenized equities onchain at institutional scale.
Tokenization, the practice of issuing traditional assets as blockchain-based tokens, has become one of Wall Street’s buzziest pursuits, but most efforts so far have centered on individual products rather than the market machinery itself.
The NYSE’s move is notable because it puts a blockchain underneath the clearing and settlement layer, the plumbing that finalizes trades, rather than just wrapping a single fund or stock in a token.
Dennis Lee, the NYSE’s head of digital issuance, said the exchange is “picking the right technology for each job,” and that while its planned platform will support equities listed across a range of blockchains, the ledger recording and settling trades needs to be fast, reliable and able to control who participates.
Emin Gün Sirer, Ava Labs’ CEO and founder, framed the deal as proof that blockchains can support not just products but the infrastructure they trade on, citing Avalanche’s “24/7 atomic settlement” and predictable costs.
The announcement adds to a frenetic race to put stocks and their underlying infrastructure onchain.
The NYSE separately tapped Blockchain.com to reach crypto investors with tokenized stocks and ETFs, while ICE and crypto exchange OKX are planning a 24/7 tokenized stock venue under an SEC exemption, and Morgan Stanley has moved to tokenize securities.
That OKX-ICE effort has hit friction, though: Every Magnificent Seven stock, including Apple and Meta, opted out of having its shares tokenized on the venue, with 67 companies in all joining them.
Research shows the appetite for tokenized stocks is real but uneven. An IMF study found tokenized stocks show genuine demand yet remain volatile and illiquid, a reminder that the infrastructure may be arriving faster than the markets to fill it.

articles.title: Bitcoin Drops Under $74K Ahead of CPI as Nvidia Sparks Stocks Volatility
articles.text:
BTC price eyes $73K amid Nvidia volatility: Three things to know in Bitcoin this week
Bitcoin price action fell to its lowest levels since mid-August as Nvidia reports added to sell-side pressure across stock-market futures.
Bitcoin (BTC) fell to about $73,500 late Sunday, its lowest level since August, as more than $1 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated ahead of this week’s US inflation reports.
Key points:
- Bitcoin hit its lowest level since Aug. 21 shortly before Sunday’s weekly close, then briefly recovered above $75,000.
- Nasdaq 100 futures swung between gains and losses after Nvidia’s board announced an investigation into whether CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort.
- US consumer and producer price reports are due Tuesday and Friday, respectively. Economist Robin Brooks said falling oil prices could lift Bitcoin.
Crypto liquidations top $1.1 billion
Bitcoin slipped below $74,000 shortly before Sunday’s weekly close, extending last week’s losses, TradingView data showed.
BTC/USD one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
About $1.12 billion in leveraged crypto positions were liquidated in the 24 hours through 9 am UTC Monday, according to CoinGlass.
Bitcoin fell below its 50-week simple moving average (SMA) of $75,492 and approached its 21-week SMA of $73,078.
BTC/USD one-day chart with 21-week and 50-week SMAs. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Bitcoin also traded below the short-term holder cost basis, which CryptoQuant put at $75,691 on Monday. The metric estimates the average cost basis of coins that last moved less than 155 days ago.
Bitcoin investor cohort cost-basis data. Source: CryptoQuant
A CryptoQuant community analyst put the cost basis for coins that last moved one to three months ago at about $79,300. The analyst said that level could act as resistance if recent buyers sell as they break even.
“In 2026, price stayed below this line for months at a time (Feb–Apr, Jun–Aug) before reclaiming it,” the analyst wrote Monday.
Bitcoin recent buyer profitability data (screenshot). Source: CryptoQuant
Trader Rekt Capital said Sunday that selling volume would need to rise before sellers showed signs of exhaustion.
“Seller Exhaustion tends to happen exactly at or very close to a Bitcoin price bottom,” Rekt Capital wrote on X.
BTC/USD one-week chart with volume data. Source: Rekt Capital on X.com
Nasdaq futures swing after Nvidia announces probe
Nvidia’s board said Sunday it had launched an independent investigation into reports that CEO Jensen Huang was targeted by a foreign intelligence effort. The board said it had no reason to believe US national security or company secrets had been compromised. China’s foreign ministry denied the spying allegations on Monday.
Nvidia futures one-hour chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Nasdaq 100 futures fell early Monday, recovered and then turned lower again ahead of the US open. S&P 500 and Dow futures were still up as Nasdaq 100 futures turned lower.
The probe followed last week’s tech sell-off, when investors weighed the outlook for AI spending and potential changes to US regulation after the midterm elections.
Nasdaq 100 futures five-minute chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Economist Mohamed El-Erian called the timing of the probe “unfortunate,” given Nvidia’s importance to the tech sector and the wider market.
“The company is systemically important for tech, markets and the economy; Investors tend to struggle to price in key-person and governance issues; and there are fluid national security and geopolitical dynamics,” he wrote in a blog post.
In Asia, South Korea’s benchmark Kospi closed down 0.8% at 5,018.85 on Monday. The exchange briefly halted trading Friday after the index fell more than 8% shortly after the open.
KOSPI one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
South Korean Vice Minister of Science and ICT Ryu Jemyung told a parliamentary budget committee Monday that he expected contracted Nvidia chip deliveries to stay on schedule.
“We expect production and the delivery schedule for contracted volumes to proceed without disruption,” he said, according to CNA.
US inflation reports loom as oil trades near $90
The US Bureau of Labor Statistics will release October’s Consumer Price Index (CPI) on Tuesday and Producer Price Index (PPI) on Friday. Both reports are due at 8:30 am ET.
Related: Here’s what happened in crypto today
Consumer prices rose 3.7% from a year earlier in September. Gasoline prices rose 9.1% from August and accounted for more than half of the monthly increase in the overall index.
US President Donald Trump told CNN on Sunday that renewed US strikes on Iran were “highly unlikely” and said the decision depended on whether Tehran signed an agreement.
West Texas Intermediate crude futures traded near $90 a barrel Monday morning.
CFDs on WTI crude oil one-day chart. Source: Cointelegraph/TradingView
Economist Robin Brooks said Sunday that the war was keeping oil prices elevated and that a decline in crude could lift Bitcoin, stocks and precious metals.
“I’m not saying that risk premium should disappear completely, but can we go to $75 a barrel? Absolutely,” he said.
Brooks forecast that Bitcoin would continue to display a negative correlation with oil as the dust settles on the US midterm elections.
“I think there’s a lot of downside for oil and I think that means upside for gold at the margin, for silver, the S&P 500 and for Bitcoin,” he continued.
“I do think that the outlook as oil prices come down, both in terms of the risk premium more broadly in the market and in terms of interest rates, it should be a relatively favorable picture.” 
Fed target-rate probability comparison for December FOMC meeting (screenshot). Source: CME Group
As markets price in 78.8% odds of the Federal Reserve raising interest rates by 25 basis points in December, per data from CME Group’s FedWatch Tool, multiple Fed officials will take to the stage in the coming days, providing insight on their stance on inflation trends and the economy.
Among them, Fed Governor Christopher Waller and Vice Chair for Supervision Michelle Bowman are both scheduled to speak on the economic outlook on Tuesday. Waller will appear at the Bank of England and its Watchers Conference 2026 in London, while Bowman will speak at the C. Peter McColough Series on International Economics in Washington.

articles.title: Strategy Buys $82M in Bitcoin, Buys Back $188M of STRC - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Strategy bought 1,036 BTC for $81.9 million between November 2 and November 8, its second straight weekly purchase, according to an SEC filing.
- The company also bought back $188.3 million of its STRC preferred stock, funding both moves by selling 2,051,348 shares of MSTR stock.
- Strategy now holds 850,364 BTC, acquired for $64.16 billion at an average of about $75,456 per coin.
Strategy bought 1,036 BTC for $81.9 million last week, its second straight weekly purchase, the company said on Monday.
The Bitcoin treasury firm paid an average of $79,012 per coin between November 2 and November 8, according to an SEC filing. It now holds 850,364 BTC, acquired for a total of $64.16 billion at an average of about $75,456 per coin.
Strategy has acquired 1,036 $BTC and repurchased $188M of $STRC. As of 11/8/26, we hold 850,364 BTC and $4.9B of USD Assets. $MSTRhttps://t.co/dNzTPPjday
— Strategy (@Strategy) November 9, 2026
The purchase is larger than the week before, when Strategy resumed buying with 811 BTC for $65.5 million after a one-week pause.
Strategy also bought back 1,887,464 shares of STRC, its variable-rate preferred stock, for $188.3 million, down from $208.2 million the previous week. It funded both the Bitcoin and the buyback by selling 2,051,348 shares of MSTR stock for $283.8 million in net proceeds, with the remaining $13.6 million going to its USD Cash account.
That marks a change from last week, when Strategy paid for its STRC buyback from USD Cash, drawing the balance down to $132.7 million. With the new proceeds, USD Cash rose to $146.2 million as of November 8.

Will Strategy hold over 1M BTC before 2027?

Strategy's preferred stock is also adjusting to a new payment schedule. Shareholders approved daily dividends on its four preferred stocks last month, starting with STRC on November 1.

articles.title: A Brazilian crypto exchange plans to show customers their money, not let them move it
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Mercado Bitcoin plans gradual November 9 account viewing, with asset detail on its website and a holdings summary in its app.
- Planned viewing would show November 2 crypto quantities and BRL valuations, while withdrawals and trading remain unavailable.
- Mercado Bitcoin says open limit orders were canceled and its Ethereum staking product earned no yield during the interruption.
Brazilian crypto exchange Mercado Bitcoin plans to restore account viewing gradually on Nov. 9, allowing customers to inspect their holdings while withdrawals and trading remain unavailable after its Nov. 2 security incident.
The exchange's recovery plan says customers will be able to see balances by asset and category on its website. Its app will offer a summary of holdings, with API access returning later. Deposits and transfers also remain unavailable, along with cards, payment services including Pix and TED, new products and account opening.
When CryptoSlate reported the shutdown on Nov. 2, the exchange had provided no reopening timetable. Mercado Bitcoin set out the Nov. 9 viewing stage in its Nov. 4 announcement, saying transaction services would follow as security checks were completed.
Customers should expect a historical view of their crypto positions. According to the exchange, the quantities shown will reflect their accounts on Nov. 2 before the incident. Their valuations in Brazilian reais will also use prices from that moment, with prices updated when trading resumes.
That means seeing a crypto balance will give customers a reference for their recorded holdings, without enabling them to sell or withdraw those assets. The displayed BRL valuation will not yet show how subsequent market price moves have changed their value.
Orders placed before the shutdown will need attention too. Mercado Bitcoin says it canceled limit orders that were open when the platform went offline on Nov. 2. Customers will be able to submit fresh orders once trading returns.
The interruption also affected yield. The exchange says it temporarily discontinued its Ethereum staking product for security reasons, so ETH in that product earned no return during the interruption. It says other staking and digital-dollar passive-income products continued accruing, with accumulated passive-income returns to be credited when those products reactivate.
The FAQ puts Pix and digital fixed-income payments in the next recovery stage, with trading and cryptoasset transfers following later. It provides no dates for those subsequent steps, leaving customers without a timetable for moving their crypto.
Before balance movements resume in those stages, all customers will have to reconfirm registration details and set new passwords through the app, the company says.
Mercado Bitcoin says customer balance records remain preserved and that it is replenishing affected assets with its own funds.
The exchange also warns customers to type its official website address directly into their browser. It says it does not send links to release balances or ask for passwords outside its platform.

articles.title: Binance, Tether and Trump-Linked Firms Face Senate Deadline
articles.text:
Binance, Tether and Trump crypto firms face Senate records deadline
Sen. Richard Blumenthal asked four crypto firms to start sending records by Nov. 30 and warned of further action if they miss the Jan. 4 deadline.
US Senator Richard Blumenthal gave Binance, Tether and two Trump-linked crypto firms until Jan. 4, 2027, to voluntarily turn over records sought in Senate inquiries.
Failure to meet the January deadline could prompt further action, he warned.
Blumenthal, the ranking Democrat and incoming chair of the Senate Permanent Subcommittee on Investigations, sent follow-up letters Thursday to Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC, the company that launched President Donald Trump’s TRUMP memecoin.
The letters asked the companies to begin turning over records by Nov. 30. The Jan. 4 deadline falls a day after Democrats are due to take control of the Senate.
Blumenthal wrote that the subcommittee would consider “alternative measures to obtain compliance” if the companies miss the January deadline. The panel’s current rules allow its chair to issue subpoenas for documents and records.
Cointelegraph sought comment from Binance, Tether, World Liberty Financial and Fight Fight Fight LLC but did not receive responses before publication.
Related: US senator probes Tether after reported deal with ex-Trump crypto adviser
Senate inquiries span sanctions and Trump’s crypto ties
In May 2025, Blumenthal opened an inquiry into potential conflicts of interest involving Trump’s crypto ventures. He sought records from both firms on their ownership, foreign investments and safeguards against conflicts of interest. World Liberty Financial’s lawyers disputed his claims and said the company had no affiliation with Fight Fight Fight LLC.
In June 2026, Blumenthal and four other Senate Democrats called for hearings into a reported $500 million deal for an Abu Dhabi investment firm to buy a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial.
In February, Blumenthal asked Binance for records on transactions linked to Iranian entities and Russia’s shadow fleet. Binance called the underlying reports false in its March reply and said that, to its knowledge, no Binance account had transacted directly with an Iran-based entity. In Thursday’s letter, Blumenthal said Binance still hadn’t turned over any of the requested records.
Blumenthal’s letter to Tether renewed requests for records on the use of USDT by sanctioned entities and on Tether’s dealings with Nxum, a consulting firm co-founded by former White House crypto adviser Bo Hines.
In September, Blumenthal released a report by the panel’s Democratic staff alleging that USDT has become a key part of Iran’s shadow banking network. Tether disputed claims that USDT provides a haven for sanctioned actors, saying it helped authorities freeze nearly $550 million in Iran-linked tokens in 2026.

articles.title: The missing step in the warning that Japan could trigger Bitcoin’s next selloff
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Ueda says substantial affiliate earnings stay invested abroad, so Japan’s income surplus does not prove immediate yen buying.
- MOF’s latest weekly release shows foreign long-term-debt buying, with October’s monthly securities data scheduled for November 10.
- Bitcoin could face different pressures from portfolio reallocation and leveraged unwinds.
Japan’s overseas profits can keep growing without the cash returning home. Bank of Japan Gov. Kazuo Ueda’s newly published International Monetary Fund lecture explains that distinction, complicating the case for treating Japan’s income surplus as an automatic source of yen buying and selling pressure on Bitcoin.
Ueda delivered the lecture on November 6, 2026, and the BOJ published it November 7. He described how substantial earnings from overseas affiliates stay invested abroad, sustaining Japan’s external income while adding to foreign direct investment.
CryptoSlate’s earlier coverage of Japanese foreign-debt selling examined how a shift toward domestic bonds could affect Bitcoin’s financing backdrop. The new lecture explains why overseas income alone cannot establish that shift.
For Bitcoin, the implications depend on what investors actually do with their money. A gradual shift toward Japanese assets could affect financing conditions; a leveraged yen carry unwind could generate much faster selling across markets. Neither can be read directly from an income-surplus headline.
In the lecture, Ueda said outward foreign direct investment has overtaken portfolio investment as Japan’s dominant capital-outflow vehicle since 2012. Direct investment concerns ownership in overseas businesses; portfolio investment concerns securities holdings.
Retained affiliate profits help explain the difference. Earnings generated abroad contribute to Japan’s primary income surplus, while reinvesting those earnings abroad is recorded as fresh direct investment. The same accounting process can therefore enlarge both income and outward investment without requiring that cash first return to Japan.
Ueda also described more active domestic investment. Yet he said Japan’s foreign-asset stock and the continuing return advantage of overseas investments would keep primary income an enduring part of its external accounts. That combination allows stronger investment at home alongside continued earnings abroad.
The latest available weekly evidence runs against a simple foreign-asset liquidation story. Japan’s Ministry of Finance (MOF) reported on November 6 that the designated Japanese reporting institutions were net buyers of foreign long-term debt and foreign equity and investment-fund shares during October 25–31.
The next checks are close. The ministry’s release schedule lists October’s monthly securities transactions for November 10 and weekly transactions covering November 1–7 for November 12, both at 8:50 a.m. Japan time. The schedule is subject to change; as of November 9, those results are still ahead.
These releases can help show whether reported foreign-security purchases or disposals persist. Their scope matters: MOF’s methodology covers designated major institutions, excludes direct investment and reserve assets, and does not capture every portfolio transaction. It also includes bond redemptions in disposals and provides no quotation-currency breakdown.
A run of net disposals would consequently be evidence about securities allocation. Establishing that the proceeds were converted into yen would require more information.
Leverage creates a faster Bitcoin exposure
A yen carry trade is a financing position. Investors borrow a lower-yielding currency to invest in higher-yielding assets denominated in other currencies, sometimes using derivatives. That differs from a Japanese company retaining an overseas subsidiary’s profits.
In an August 2024 analysis, researchers at the Bank for International Settlements (BIS) described how deleveraging and increased margin requirements appeared to amplify market turbulence, with yen-funded carry positions particularly exposed. A stronger yen can make an unhedged yen borrowing position more costly to repay, while higher margins can force investors to find cash or cut exposure.
The researchers said that episode’s crypto losses suggested retail margin calls and possible forced closures of otherwise unrelated positions. Those historical findings illustrate a possible transmission channel, rather than establishing forced Bitcoin selling now.
The distinction changes what would strengthen the risk case. Persistent foreign-security disposals would support an allocation shift. Sharper yen moves accompanied by funding and margin stress would be more relevant to a leveraged unwind. Continued outward investment and retained earnings would weaken the claim that overseas profits must immediately drain into yen.

articles.title: Microsoft-Backed Space and Time Launches Platform to Let AI Agents Verify Private Data - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Space and Time has launched Space and Time Enterprise, a platform that lets businesses prove calculations on private data are correct without exposing the underlying records.
- Launch partners include Maple Finance, Indomobil, Trenez and The Data Foundation, and businesses can run the software on their own servers without operating a blockchain.
- AI agents "don't need unrestricted access to the records behind every calculation," Nate Holiday, CEO of Space and Time developer MakeInfinite Labs, told Decrypt.
Space and Time, a Microsoft-backed blockchain data project, has launched a platform designed to let businesses use private data in AI tools without handing over the underlying records, the company announced on Monday.
Space and Time Enterprise lets companies prove that calculations made on their private data are correct, so that AI applications, auditors and other stakeholders can check the results without accessing the database itself. Launch partners include onchain asset manager Maple Finance, Indonesian vehicle maker and distributor Indomobil, Oracle software consultancy Trenez and AI data network The Data Foundation.
"Businesses want AI agents to execute workflows using that information, but those agents don't need unrestricted access to the records behind every calculation," Nate Holiday, CEO of MakeInfinite Labs, the original developer of Space and Time, told Decrypt.
The stakes are high, he argued. "The potential cost to a business is the overall value of the business," Holiday said. "Giving AI tools unrestricted access to data creates another avenue of exposure."
Holiday said the company is working with customers in industries including construction, engineering and manufacturing that want to rebuild their systems around AI, so that agents, reporting tools and compliance teams can work from the same business records and check the calculations they rely on.
Proof of SQL and the SXT token
The platform is built on Proof of SQL, Space and Time's patented technology for proving that database queries were computed correctly. It already works with Google Cloud's BigQuery, and businesses can now run it on their own servers without operating a blockchain, buying specialized hardware or relying on an outside proving service, according to the company.
With GPU acceleration, supported queries over millions of rows can be run and proven in under a second, Holiday said, though actual performance depends on the query, hardware and dataset.
The technology proves that a calculation was carried out correctly on a given set of records, but it cannot tell whether those records were accurate to begin with. "An incorrect entry still needs to be caught through the business's data controls," Holiday said, "but verification gives those controls a much stronger foundation: evidence of which data was used and whether it was processed correctly."
Space and Time raised $20 million in 2022 in a strategic funding round led by M12, Microsoft's venture fund. Last year, Grayscale launched a trust giving investors exposure to SXT, the token that powers Space and Time's blockchain. Earlier this year, the company launched Dreamspace, an AI-powered tool built with Microsoft's Azure AI services that lets users create and deploy onchain apps without writing code.
Space and Time also runs SXT Chain, a decentralized network that supplies verifiable data to DeFi, tokenized assets and stablecoins. Asked whether enterprise customers would create demand for SXT, Holiday said businesses could deploy the product in their own environment, and that the network would come into play as their applications "need to connect to onchain markets," with those workloads paid for through Space and Time.
The company's cryptography is also used elsewhere. Microsoft's Nova project includes Blitzar, Space and Time's cryptographic acceleration library, and the team's work on a commitment scheme called Dory contributed to a16z crypto's Jolt proof system, Holiday said.

articles.title: Weekly Bitcoin ETF Outflows Hit $1.3B, Most Since June
articles.text:
Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.3B in biggest weekly outflow since late June
Investors pulled a net $1.21 billion from BlackRock’s IBIT last week as Bitcoin fell below $76,000 and US technology stocks sold off.
US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $1.28 billion in net outflows last week, their largest weekly withdrawals since late June.
The withdrawals brought the funds’ net outflows for the year to about $919 million, according to SoSoValue. The funds had already posted $515 million in net outflows in October.
Bitcoin fell below $76,000 last week as traders digested the fallout from Binance’s $6.3 billion hack, uncertainty after the US midterm elections and a sell-off in technology stocks.
BlackRock’s IBIT leads Bitcoin ETF outflows
BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT), the world’s largest spot Bitcoin ETF by assets, recorded $1.21 billion in net outflows last week, according to Farside Investors data.
The withdrawals extended IBIT’s losing streak to six consecutive trading sessions, with approximately $1.44 billion pulled from the fund since Oct. 30. IBIT accounted for about 95% of the weekly total reported by SoSoValue.
IBIT recorded net outflows for six consecutive trading sessions through Friday, bringing withdrawals since Oct. 30 to about $1.44 billion.
Fidelity’s Wise Origin Bitcoin Fund (FBTC) drew about $93 million in net inflows for the week, despite losing nearly $200 million Thursday.
Bitfire flags further downside risk for Bitcoin
Shifting expectations for US interest rates, uncertainty after the midterms and weakness in technology stocks weighed on crypto markets, Bitfire Research said in a statement shared with Cointelegraph.
Bitfire said investors were also reassessing whether Congress could pass the CLARITY Act before year-end.
Related: Bitcoin price dips under $75K as crypto markets miss tech-stock rebound
Bitfire cited a Crypto Fear & Greed Index reading of 25 and a negative Coinbase Premium, which indicates Bitcoin was trading at a discount on Coinbase relative to the indicator’s benchmark.
Bitfire described the market as being in a “breakdown and bottom-seeking phase,” pointing to upcoming US inflation data and signals from the Federal Reserve as factors to watch. It said that a sustained break below the $74,400–$75,000 support range could lead to further selling.
Bitcoin traded at $74,049 at publication, below the lower end of that range. It was down 5% over seven days and 2.3% over 24 hours, according to CoinGecko.

articles.title: Coinbase Joins Circle, Ripple With Final OCC Approval for Federal Trust Bank Charter - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- Coinbase has received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency to charter Coinbase National Trust Company.
- The charter brings Coinbase's institutional crypto custody business under a single federal regulator, building on its existing New York trust charter.
- Coinbase is the latest crypto firm to win a national trust charter this year, after Circle and Ripple, as banking groups challenge the approvals in court.
Coinbase has received final approval from the Office of the Comptroller of the Currency (OCC) to charter Coinbase National Trust Company, the crypto exchange said on Monday.
The OCC approved the application last Friday, according to Coinbase. The firm said the charter will let it expand its custody business, which holds digital assets on behalf of institutional clients, under a federal regulatory framework.
"Custody is foundational to our business," the company said, describing itself as the leading crypto custodian globally. The charter will "bring clear and consistent federal uniformity" to its custody operations, it added.
"Trusted custody is essential for bringing more of the financial system onchain," Coinbase CEO Brian Armstrong tweeted on Monday, calling the trust company "another step for building that foundation."
Trusted custody is essential for bringing more of the financial system onchain.
Coinbase National Trust Company is another step for building that foundation. https://t.co/35K2yC3xpj
— Brian Armstrong (@brian_armstrong) November 9, 2026
Coinbase has offered regulated custody since 2018, when its Coinbase Custody Trust Company won a limited purpose trust charter from the New York Department of Financial Services. The new national trust company builds on that foundation while bringing its trust activities into a consistent federal framework, Coinbase said.
The approval comes seven months after the OCC gave Coinbase conditional approval in April, when the company said it was not becoming a commercial bank and would not take retail deposits or engage in fractional reserve banking. Coinbase first applied for the charter last year.
The crypto charter wave
Coinbase joins a growing list of crypto firms with national trust charters. Circle won final approval in July for a trust bank to manage the reserves behind its USDC stablecoin, and Ripple received final approval last month for a trust bank behind its RLUSD stablecoin.
Others are still awaiting final approval. Jack Dorsey's Block has applied for a charter to custody Bitcoin in September, Kraken parent Payward filed its own application in May, and a trust company linked to Trump family-backed World Liberty Financial won conditional approval in August for a charter tied to its USD1 stablecoin, Reuters reported.
The approvals have drawn opposition. Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA) has argued that the OCC's crypto charter approvals, including Coinbase's, are illegal, and the Independent Community Bankers of America has sued the OCC in an effort to stop crypto firms from entering banking through what it describes as a side door.

articles.title: Two Bitcoin miners reported nearly $2 billion in profit. The biggest boost wasn’t cash
articles.text:
Quick Take
- Core Scientific and TeraWulf reported nearly $1.9 billion in combined Q3 net income alongside $1.76 billion of pretax non-cash gains.
- Core earned $72 million in operating income, while TeraWulf lost $88 million despite hosting supplying most revenue at both companies.
- Their nine-month cash flows show construction drawing on financing and balance-sheet resources.
Core Scientific and TeraWulf reported nearly $1.9 billion of combined third-quarter profit as they shifted from Bitcoin mining toward data-center hosting for AI customers. Their earnings included $1.76 billion of pretax non-cash gains from revaluing financial instruments.
The November 5 Core Scientific disclosure and November 6 TeraWulf disclosure show different operating outcomes for the quarter ended September 30, 2026. Core earned $72 million in operating income under U.S. accounting rules; TeraWulf recorded an $88 million operating loss. Core's operating result itself included a $19 million digital-asset fair-value gain. Hosting now supplies most of both companies' revenue, following their shift from Bitcoin mining toward computing leases. Assessing whether the conversions fund themselves requires the separate cash-flow and financing disclosures.
How non-cash gains lifted Core Scientific and TeraWulf profits
Core’s $1,178 million consolidated net income and TeraWulf’s $710 million add up to approximately $1.89 billion.
In Core's filing, the $1,034 million revaluation gain comprised $964 million on legacy Tranche 1 and Tranche 2 warrants, $69 million on the liability portion of an AMD warrant and $1 million on contingent value rights. Legacy instruments supplied the largest component of Core's gain.
Warrants give holders rights to buy shares. Core's AMD warrant accompanied July customer leases, with its issuance value recorded as an incentive reducing future lease revenue. Its liability portion is remeasured through earnings. Core attributed changes in its broader warrant and contingent-value line primarily to stock-price changes.
TeraWulf's $728 million gain came from revaluing Google warrants issued in exchange for credit support covering certain Fluidstack lease obligations. The credit support can help finance projects. Remeasurement raises reported earnings through a non-cash accounting entry.
The revaluation gains enter earnings before tax, while the net-income figures also reflect tax effects and other gains. Core also recorded a $106.5 million tax benefit, primarily from releasing part of a valuation allowance associated with its Polaris acquisition. TeraWulf recorded a $95 million gain on selling its Abernathy joint-venture stake.
The difference also reaches per-share results: Core reported $3.42 basic earnings versus $0.47 diluted, while TeraWulf reported $1.42 basic earnings and a $0.03 diluted loss. The diluted calculations include warrant-gain reversals in the earnings used per share, alongside share-count adjustments.
Hosting growth is visible in both companies' sales. Core's colocation revenue reached $215 million out of $233 million in total sales, up from $137 million in the preceding quarter. Colocation gross profit was $128 million at a reported 60% margin.
TeraWulf generated $63 million of high-performance computing (HPC) lease revenue, approximately 83% of its $76 million total. Its $11 million HPC segment profit excludes expenses including corporate overhead and depreciation that enter consolidated operating results, giving it a different expense allocation from Core's colocation gross profit.
Construction funding shows up elsewhere
For the nine months ended September 30, Core generated $296 million of operating cash while spending $1,495 million on property, plant and equipment and another $677 million on asset acquisitions. Net financing cash inflow was $3,200 million.
Over that same nine-month period, TeraWulf used $179 million of operating cash and spent $2,231 million on plant and equipment purchases and deposits. It received $1,010 million of net financing cash, including approximately $1,200 million from common-stock issuance.
Core says conversions for hosting customer CoreWeave are largely funded by that customer. Development under its AMD and other cloud-customer arrangements will require additional external financing. It plans project-level bond financing. Management says existing liquidity plus anticipated funding sources support planned development and operating needs.
TeraWulf's Abernathy sale supplied $250 million of cash during Q3, distinct from the accounting gain; further installments remained expected. After quarter-end, it increased revolving-credit commitments to about $400 million, with an additional conditional, uncommitted $150 million expansion option. Its post-quarter November 4 Google credit support for leases with customer Anthropic concerns anticipated project financing. The Fluidstack warrants behind Q3's gain relate to a separate arrangement.
For the next phase, the operating split provides a more useful starting point than the combined profit: Core has reached positive operating income, while TeraWulf still reports an operating loss. Delivered hosting capacity, cash collections and financing commitments will determine how much of the construction bill the growing businesses can carry.

articles.title: Zcash Developers Propose 20-Second Blocks After NU7 Upgrade
articles.text:
Zcash devs propose another block time cut days after NU7 upgrade
The proposed reduction aims to shorten transaction confirmation times and improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps.
Zcash developers have proposed reducing the blockchain’s target block interval from 25 seconds to 20 seconds, seeking faster transaction confirmations days after activating the NU7 upgrade.
On Sunday, developers ValarDragon and Evan Forbes submitted a draft Zcash Improvement Proposal (ZIP) on the Zcash community forum, saying that they want the change to be included in the next community poll and considered for the upcoming NU7.1 network upgrade.
The reduction would shorten the expected wait for initial transaction confirmations. According to the proposal, this would improve the user experience for point-of-sale payments, exchange deposits and cross-chain swaps.
The developers said the change would not increase the network’s overall daily capacity for private transactions. The proposal would also preserve Zcash’s existing issuance schedule, despite blocks being produced more frequently.
The proposal comes just days after Zcash’s NU7 upgrade went live. On Friday, the NU7 upgrade was activated on the mainnet, cutting the network’s target block interval from 75 seconds to 25 seconds.
The upgrade also introduced a Network Sustainability Mechanism designed to recycle a portion of transaction fees into future mining rewards while preserving Zcash’s 21 million ZEC supply cap.
Related: Zcash grants group offers $124M compromise as governance backlash grows

articles.title: Trump Says He Knows 'Nothing' About World Liberty Financial as He Defends UAE Ties - Decrypt
articles.text:
In brief
- U.S. President Donald Trump said he knows "nothing" about World Liberty Financial when asked about the crypto firm's UAE-linked investors in a post-midterms interview.
- Asked why he does not divest, Trump said his sons run the business and that conflicts of interest are a problem "for every president."
- A UAE-backed firm agreed to buy a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial for $500 million days before Trump's inauguration, prompting accusations of corruption.
U.S. President Donald Trump has defended his family's stake in crypto venture World Liberty Financial, saying he knows "nothing" about the firm despite being a co-owner, in an interview after last week's midterm elections.
Asked by columnist Ross Douthat why his co-ownership of a company partly owned by investors linked to the United Arab Emirates government was different from the kind of arrangement he would call corrupt if it involved the Biden family, Trump replied: "Here's the difference [... ] I'm gonna tell you why. Because I know nothing about it," according to a transcript published by CBS News.
Pressed on why he did not simply divest, Trump said most of his money is managed by Wall Street firms through index funds, and that his sons run the family business. "It's hard to say to them, 'Don't do anything anymore for four years because I'm president,'" he said.
When Douthat asked whether foreign investors in the company believe they are buying influence, Trump said: "I don't know." He argued that conflicts of interest have dogged presidents "going back to George Washington," adding that past presidents "own something, whatever crypto was at the time."
"There's crypto, and before that there was oil," Trump said, adding that, "every president has had this problem."
"I'm a bigger name than other presidents, whether we like it or not," Trump said.
World Liberty's UAE ties
World Liberty Financial, which Eric Trump announced in August 2024, issues the WLFI governance token and the USD1 stablecoin. In January, it launched World Liberty Markets, a lending and borrowing platform built on DeFi protocol Dolomite.
Its UAE links have drawn scrutiny from Democrats. Aryam Investment, a UAE-backed entity tied to the country's national security adviser, Sheikh Tahnoon bin Zayed, agreed to buy a 49% stake in World Liberty Financial for $500 million four days before Trump's January 2025 inauguration, Decrypt reported in February, citing The Wall Street Journal. The deal, signed by Eric Trump on World Liberty's behalf, reportedly preceded the administration's reversal of restrictions on advanced AI chip sales to the UAE. A World Liberty spokesperson said at the time that neither Trump nor his Middle East envoy, Steve Witkoff, had "any involvement whatsoever" in the transaction, ABC News reported. Sen. Chris Murphy (D-CT) described the arrangement in February as "potentially criminal conduct." Trump has previously said he was not aware of the deal.
The company's UAE ties have also surfaced in its legal battle with Tron founder Justin Sun. Sun's lawyers asked a federal court to sanction World Liberty, alleging the firm delayed disclosing UAE ownership that could defeat federal jurisdiction over his lawsuit. World Liberty has called Sun's legal campaign a "meritless PR stunt."
The Trump family's financial stake in the venture is set out in World Liberty's own disclosures. DT Marks DEFI LLC, an entity affiliated with Trump and certain family members, owns about 38% of the holding company behind World Liberty Financial, holds 22.5 billion WLFI tokens, and is entitled to 75% of the net proceeds from WLFI token sales, according to the company. A separate Trump-affiliated entity has an indirect claim on interest earned on the reserves backing USD1. The disclosures state that no member of the Trump family is an officer, director or employee of World Liberty, though Trump's sons have remained involved with the company, Decrypt reported earlier this year.
