articles.title: S&P 500 futures are little changed as traders brace for crucial consumer inflation report: Live updates
articles.text:
U.S. stock futures largely traded near the flatline Monday night as traders awaited a pivotal consumer inflation report.
S&P 500 futures were marginally higher, while futures tied to the Dow Jones Industrial Average were up just 18 points. Nasdaq-100 futures added 0.2%.
In Asia, South Korea's Kospi surged 4.3% Tuesday. Japan's Nikkei 225 added 2.89%, while Australia's S&P/ASX 200 gained 1.27%. Hong Kong's Hang Seng Index rose 0.42% and mainland's CSI 300 added 0.26%.
During the regular U.S. trading day, the Dow Industrials gained 1,104 points, or 2.2%, while the S&P 500 popped about 2.4%. The Nasdaq Composite rose 2.7%. Monday's rally came after a rocky week for markets, in which traders grew concerned of an impending slowdown in data center buildouts after Democrats posted big victories in the midterm elections.
While the tech sector rebounded in Monday's regular trading, Nvidia sat out the rally.
Shares of the chipmaker slid 4% after Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang admitted on Sunday to having an affair with a woman who U.S. intelligence officials, according to The New York Times, say is a spy for China's Ministry of State Security. The company's board of directors also launched an independent internal investigation, pointing to recent reporting that Huang "has been the target of a foreign intelligence effort."
Oil prices also fell on Monday, lending the market support. The U.S. West Texas Intermediate futures settled down more than 4%, while Brent crude futures slid more than 5%.
Investors are awaiting the October consumer price index report due on Tuesday. Economists polled by Dow Jones see headline CPI growing at a rate of 0.3% and core CPI, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, rising 0.2% from the prior month.
This would mark a deceleration from September's readings, when headline CPI grew 0.6% and core CPI advanced 0.3%.
"We think the slowdown in core CPI will stem from a reversion of shelter prices, primarily owners' equivalent rents and lodging away from home. Similarly, the stabilization in diesel prices should help to quell price pressures in energy-intensive goods," wrote Christopher Hodge, chief economist of the U.S. at Natixis CIB Americas.
Annual figures will not be provided for Tuesday's report because of the 2025 government shutdown. At that time, the Bureau of Labor Statistics was unable to collect some data which means there isn't a comparable figure for the index.

articles.title: CNBC's The China Connection newsletter: Wall Street dips in again. What needs to go right
articles.text:
Hi, this is Evelyn, writing to you from Beijing. Welcome to the latest edition of The China Connection — a snapshot of what I'm seeing and hearing from local businesses.
China has long wanted global investors' money to bolster the prominence of its domestic stock market. Giving foreigners that access hasn't happened overnight. Why are Wall Street firms still trying?
The big story
Global investment firms are eyeing mainland China not just for its tech stocks, but for the millions of affluent people who could become their clients.
Mainland Chinese with more than $125,000 in bankable assets hold a combined $27 trillion in wealth, according to financial analytics firm Crisil Coalition Greenwich. And the millionaire population has surged — to nearly 4 million, up from 1 million a decade ago.
On the heels of getting Beijing's approval to establish a wholly-owned securities company, Citi's CEO Jane Fraser is kicking off the U.S. bank's annual China conference this week in Shanghai. It's the latest U.S. financial firm to benefit from China's pledge after the Trump-Xi summit in September to approve applications from all foreign financial institutions to operate in the country.
Also headlining Citi's China conference in person is Anna Wintour, former editor-in-chief of Vogue. Condé Nast did not respond to a request for comment.
"The environment is meaningfully more open than it was a decade ago, although it remains highly regulated," said Nuno Cordeiro, head of wealth management, and Fabio Zheng, senior product manager, wealth management, at Crisil Coalition Greenwich.
They pointed out that compared to past years, the property market slowdown has also created greater demand for diversification and advisory services.
"The question today is no longer whether foreign firms can participate. It is whether they can generate sufficient scale and returns within those constraints," they said in an email. "Consequently, most successful strategies combine greater local presence with partnerships that provide access to domestic distribution."
Localization
Franklin Templeton, which oversees $1.8 trillion in assets, and ChinaAMC, which manages over 3.1 trillion yuan ($462.5 billion), signed a strategic partnership on Oct. 28 for sharing market insights and jointly developing products.
They are already working on co-branded ETFs across Hong Kong, U.S. and European fund structures.
The deal goes both ways.
"Just as a lot of international investors [are] interested in China investment, Chinese investors are looking for global investment vehicles," Sherrie Dai, managing director, global capital, at ChinaAMC, told me.
A Hong Kong-listed ETF launched with Franklin Templeton on Sept. 29 holds around 40% U.S. stocks and 60% Hong Kong-listed ones.
Such products could, in six to 12 months, meet Beijing's threshold for letting mainland China-based investors participate, Dai said. Her company is also launching products for investors in Brazil to allocate to Chinese tech companies.
Since early 2025, DeepSeek's AI breakthroughs and other Chinese tech advances have gained foreign investors' attention. U.S.-based Roundhill Investments included China stocks in its thematic ETFs focusing on humanoids, memory chips or other tech — but exposure to mainland-listed names may sometimes come through derivatives.
Performance hasn't helped. Chinese stocks have tumbled this year, significantly underperforming their U.S. peers.
On the China business front, foreign financial firms have also struggled. In late 2025, BlackRock decided to shut down its three-year-old China Innovation Fund, which only had $31.7 million in net assets. Vanguard in 2023 sold its stake in a mainland China mutual fund operator to majority owner Ant Group.
Peter Alexander, founder and managing director of Z-Ben Advisors in Shanghai, attributed part of the challenge to "micromanagement" from headquarters outside China.
"Global groups have failed in China due solely to their inability to make the necessary adjustments to how it is they operate to best fit the Chinese market," he said.
Reducing volatility
Capital controls, a state-dominated system and varying levels of investor communication contribute to a mainland Chinese stock market quite different from that of the U.S.
State-linked funds, known as the "National Team," often step up stock purchases to limit market sell-offs.
Last week, amid reports of a pause in new Chinese IPOs, a senior financial regulator warned in a speech that too much capital concentration in tech can drive up leverage, while crowding out traditional industries.
Such headlines can support short-term stock market gains. But for longer-term investors, who might not be able to buy in immediately, rapid price surges raise the risk that they are "buying at the top," said Liqian Ren, a quantitative manager at U.S.-based fund manager WisdomTree.
High volatility means those investors can only hold a certain amount of Chinese stocks due to perceived risk, she said. The market "becomes a trading vehicle. That's not necessarily good for China."
"Ultimately you need the market to figure it out. You need the punishment to come from the market."
Need to know
China expands overseas mining stakes, tightening grip on critical minerals
Chinese mineral acquisitions abroad in the first three quarters of the year along marked the highest annually since at least 2018, according to Rhodium Group. That adds to the existing rare earths leverage Beijing has used in U.S. trade tensions. China is also demanding lower tariffs before buying more U.S. agricultural goods.
What the Democratic midterms sweep changes for U.S.-China relations
Democrats taking power from Republicans in Congress raises risks for U.S.-China tensions around Taiwan, while hardening tech competition, analysts said. Russia and China may feel the need to test the U.S. if they feel Trump is on "his way out," according to Robert Kagan, senior fellow at the Brookings Institution.
Moonshot turned to Europe for Nvidia Blackwell access amid U.S. China curbs, sources tell CNBC
Deals have been discussed this year for Moonshot to rent capacity from neoclouds hosting Nvidia graphics processing units, or GPUs, at facilities in Europe, four people familiar with the matter said. Meanwhile in Asia, reports of a prison sentencing in South Korea reflect the growing AI chip talent war.
Coming up
Nov. 10: Trade data
Nov. 10 - 13: Citi China Conference in Shanghai and Shenzhen
Nov. 13: Extended Singles Day shopping festival wraps up
Nov. 16: Retail sales, industrial production and fixed-asset investment

articles.title: Trump says Jensen Huang told him Monday he didn't know paramour 'was a spy'
articles.text:
President Donald Trump said he spoke to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang on Monday, and that Huang denied knowing that the woman he admitted having an extramarital affair with "was a spy" for China.
Trump told reporters at the White House that he was "amazed" by the allegations against Huang, which led Nvidia's board to initiate an independent investigation.
Trump suggested he had only recently learned of allegations that Megaspeed International executive Alice Huang was a Chinese spy.
"I didn't hear about it then, but a lot of people have heard about it, and Jensen totally denies that," Trump said.
"I asked him today because I did speak to him today just to see if he's feeling all right. 'How you doing?'" Trump said.
"And I asked him about that, and he ... said he had absolutely no idea that the person in question was a spy," the president said. "I asked him that question: 'Did you have any idea that she was a spy?' He said, 'I had no idea that she was a spy.' "
"I really believe him," Trump said.
The New York Times on Oct. 29 reported that Alice Huang had been eyed by U.S. spy agencies "for possibly steering advanced Nvidia A.I. chips to China," and that "American officials had concluded she was a Chinese intelligence asset, funneling information to Beijing."
The Times reported that about a year ago, Trump was briefed about the intelligence findings "and chose not to do anything with the information." The newspaper noted that Trump has been reluctant to disrupt chip sales by Nvdia, which are boosting the U.S. stock market.
On Friday, The Times reported that a memo that circulated last spring among top Trump administration policymakers "cited intelligence that a Chinese businesswoman who had a close relationship with Nvidia's chief executive was a spy for China's Ministry of State Security."
The Times said the memo reported that Alice Huang was recruited to collect intelligence on the Nvidia CEO "as part of a drive by Beijing's top spy agency to learn more about American A.I. chips and potentially influence the company to push for its most advanced chips to be made available to China."
"I've been reading a little bit about it over a period of time, but not too long ago," Trump said Monday. "We'll look into it. I know the FBI is looking into it in terms of something else, and I think that he'll be in good shape."
Trump on Monday said of Jensen Huang, "He's suffering greatly."
"I believe he's suffering greatly. I read his statement, and I believe he's suffering greatly, more so because of his family, his wife, who he loves, and his family. But he is definitely suffering."
Asked if he would bring up the issue involving Huang with Chinese President Xi Jinping when the two leaders meet next week at the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation summit in Shenzhen, China, Trump said, "I don't think so."
"I mean, maybe I'm sure President Xi will ask me about it," Trump said. "I just know Jensen very well. I just think he's a very honorable, honorable man. I mean ... he built a great company, American company, and I think he's a very honorable guy, and I feel very confident that he'll be in good shape."
Trump's comments came as a Los Angeles law firm filed a class-action shareholder lawsuit against Nvidia and Huang in federal court in San Jose, California.
The Rosen Law Firm's suit alleges the defendants made false or misleading statements about his affair with Huang and Nvidia's relationship with Megaspeed, which presented a material risk to the company's reputation and business prospects.

articles.title: 3 unexpected reasons the October jobs report was so strong
articles.text:
A little-noticed category in Friday's blockbuster jobs report is challenging the consensus view about job losses caused by artificial intelligence.
At least for now, the data suggests the U.S. is gaining jobs as a result of the AI boom, not losing them.
And another category suggests the strong jobs numbers could have some staying power.
Nonfarm payrolls grew by 165,000 jobs in October, according to the Friday report from the Bureau of Labor Statistics. It was a surprising surge in hiring that blew way past Wall Street's expectations. Economists polled by Dow Jones had forecast growth of just 59,000 for the month.
Here are three surprising things you might have missed from the report.
Consulting
Hiring for consultants surged in the month, sending the profession's total head count to a fresh record.
The labor force for management, scientific and technical consultants expanded by 17,300 jobs between September and October, the largest month-over-month increase in nearly two years. This category is a subset of the professional and business services sector tracked by BLS and accounted for 25% of the entire sector's gains for the month.
What's more, this workforce has grown by more than 45,000 jobs over the past year. That gain pushed the total employee base for these types of workers past 1.9 million for the first time on record, according to BLS data.
Hiring in the industry had largely stalled since 2023 following years of rapid expansion during the pandemic. Wall Street has questioned if the rise of artificial intelligence will curb demand for these services.
Those fears have led shares of consulting firm Gartner to lose more than half of their value over the past three years. Accenture and FTI Consulting have dropped about 18% and 9% over that period, even as the S&P 500 has climbed roughly 74%.
Now, some economists are speculating that the recent jump could be driven by businesses hiring consultants to help them adopt AI. Gartner forecast in September that worldwide AI spending would total $2.7 trillion in 2026, a nearly 50% increase year over year.
"The AI buildout and corporate interests to increase utilization will keep the technical consultants employed," said Jeffrey Roach, chief economist at LPL Financial.
Roach called the consulting sector a bright spot in October that is "worth watching." He noted that these jobs also saw double-digit growth in the late 1990s, as firms raced to implement new internet technology into their businesses.
So far, data suggests that AI may be adding more jobs to the labor market than it is taking away through automation. An assessment by Moody's Analytics found that AI has created a net 786,000 jobs since ChatGPT launched in November 2022, driven in part by data center construction.
"Wasn't AI supposed to destroy jobs? The most dystopian scenarios even called for mass unemployment," Mark Zandi, Moody's chief economist, wrote in a social media post on Monday. "That risk hasn't gone away, and AI-driven productivity gains could still shift into a higher gear. But for now, AI is adding to job growth, not subtracting from it."
Temporary hires
Hiring of temporary workers also drove growth, which could signal that the labor market is heating up.
The subsector's payrolls grew by 18,600 in October, one of its largest month-over-month increases since 2022. This category is another part of the professional and business services sector and accounted for 27% of the sector's gains for the month.
The total size of this workforce is still well below record highs set in 2022. But headcount has grown roughly 3% since December and now sits at levels last seen in April 2025, the month that President Donald Trump's rollout of his plan for steep tariffs put corporate America on alert.
Economists see temporary hiring as a leading indicator in the labor market. Conventional wisdom suggests that companies that hire new workers on a short-term basis often transition them to full-time roles later.
That could be what's happening here, but the fact that the end of the year is approaching makes it harder to tell. The boost could be a result of hiring as the holiday shopping season approaches — and if employers are staffing up for the holidays, they are less likely to retain those workers when January rolls around. Such hiring hasn't typically happened this early, but the season creeps earlier each year. The BLS adjusts its numbers to account for seasonal trends, but won't immediately make an adjustment if the trend is changing.
One hint that holiday hiring may be shifting comes in a separate category of workers: couriers and messengers. This is another area that acts as a barometer for holiday labor demand, and just over one out of every 10 new jobs in the month was in this category.
That category "bears watching for reversal in the months ahead," said Jason Pride, chief of investment strategy and research at Glenmede, a wealth manager.
Election spending
Hiring related to political campaigns in the final weeks of an expensive election cycle could have also boosted payrolls.
Employment in political organizations has historically spiked heading into midterm or presidential elections, according to a BLS analysis. Staffing levels tend to peak in October of those years, the data shows. Nonfarm payrolls expanded in the months before the 2018 and 2022 midterm elections.
But the vast size of campaign coffers this cycle may have translated into more jobs than before.
The 2026 congressional election is slated to go down in history as the most expensive midterm on record, according to an analysis from OpenSecrets, a money-in-politics watchdog group. Billions of dollars spent on campaigns may have translated into paid gigs that involve door knocking, phone banking or other election-related work.

articles.title: Skydance outlines its $6 billion in planned cost savings. Here's the breakdown
articles.text:
Skydance is pulling back the curtain on how it plans to achieve at least $6 billion in cost savings in the next three years.
"By combining two global streaming services, two film and TV studio groups, two television portfolios, and overlapping corporate functions, we can reduce duplicative spend across an expense base of more than $50 billion," the company wrote in a letter to shareholders Monday as part of Paramount Skydance's third-quarter earnings release.
Skydance, the company formed by the combination of Paramount Skydance and Warner Bros. Discovery, said it projects at least $2.2 billion in cost reductions from eliminating "redundant back-office and corporate functions," including eliminating management layers and ramping the use of artificial intelligence. Those savings also account for "rationalizing" its office footprint.
Skydance expects at least $1 billion in savings from streamlining marketing and promotional spending. And around $1.4 billion in savings will come from unifying its streaming businesses and broadcast architecture and integrating back-end technology.
A final $1.4 billion in savings will be tied to "optimizing third-party spend," eliminating overlapping expenses, and consolidating purchasing decisions to one centralized group, Skydance said.
"We are confident in achieving these savings, drawing on our playbook from Paramount," the company wrote. "That program is on track to achieve over $2.7 billion in run-rate efficiencies by the end of 2026."
Some of that cost-cutting has already begun.
Last month, Skydance began offering voluntary buyouts to employees ahead of official layoffs. At the same time, the company adopted a five-day-per-week in-office policy. Additionally, last week saw the departure of eight executives — four from Warner Bros. and four from Paramount.
The company has previously said it plans to eventually merge the Paramount+ and HBO Max streaming services into a single platform.
On Monday, Skydance said it would take the first step toward that goal early next year, offering a bundle of the streaming services "at an even greater value."
Co-CEO Ynon Kreiz told investors during the company's earnings call that Skydance is also looking for ways to optimize its content budget. The company spends more than $30 billion annually on shows and films.
"As one company, we can make smarter choices about how we distribute and monetize both new content and library content," Kreiz said.
Skydance noted that it's expecting a $200 million headwind in the fourth quarter from theatrical underperformances at Warner Bros. studio related to already launched titles and upcoming releases.
The company will also utilize AI to speed up production and decrease costs to make films, co-CEO and chairman David Ellison said on the call.
"We think these tools will help unlock more original storytelling by being able to make the budget more digestible to be able to take that amount of risk," Ellison said.
The updates came alongside third-quarter results for the legacy Paramount Skydance company that included revenue of $7.03 billion, which was roughly in line with StreetAccount estimates of $7.04 billion, and adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of $1 billion, topping StreetAccount estimates of $913.5 million.
However, adjusted earnings per share of 45 cents were not immediately comparable to StreetAccount EPS estimates.
The results don't include the impact of the Warner Bros. Discovery acquisition, which closed after the end of the third quarter.
Skydance detailed business units of the combined entity, including studios, direct-to-consumer and TV, and said it will provide full-year guidance during its fourth-quarter earnings report early next year.
"Going forward, we will provide guidance on an annual basis, as we prioritize long-term value creation, which we believe will be more consistent with our strategic approach," the company told shareholders. "We will continue to provide quarterly updates, including certain forward-looking commentary where applicable, which will give investors visibility into our near-term progress of the business."

articles.title: Tokenization platform Securitize gains 10% postmarket on Q3 results, move into asset-backed finance
articles.text:
Tokenization platform Securitize climbed about 10% postmarket after reporting third quarter growth alongside increased operating expenses, and announcing an expansion into asset-backed finance through a strategic acquisition.
Miami-based Securitize, which made its public market debut in July, operates in the relatively new corner of the crypto equity universe involved in institutional tokenization infrastructure. Tokenized assets on the platform grew 9% in the third quarter, to $4.8 billion, from the same period a year ago. Aggregate transaction volume rose 20% from a year ago, to $4.3 billion. Revenue of $11.5 million was up 28% from last year.
The growth came as bullish sentiment around tokenization gained traction throughout the third quarter, ahead of the Security and Exchange Commission formalizing the long awaited Innovation Exemption on Sept. 17, which created a temporary pathway for trading of certain tokenized stocks and strengthened the regulatory outlook.
Profitability is still meaningfully below year-ago levels, due in part to costs associated with going public over the summer, as well as the scaling up of the tokenization business at an active time for the entire sector, Securitize CEO Carlos Domingo told CNBC in an exclusive interview.
Stronger compliance
Securitize reinforced "certain areas of the company like finance, compliance, legal [and] cybersecurity," which increased corporate costs "compared to a year ago when we were privately held," Domingo said. "We're in in a very good position. The adjusted EBITDA … is improving significantly from previous quarters."
Securitize reported an adjusted EBITDA loss of $2 million, compared with positive adjusted EBITDA of $3.6 million a year ago, better than a $5.5 million loss in the second quarter. The company posted a 183% increase in operating costs and expenses.
Also on Monday, the Securitize board authorized a $50 million share buyback and announced the acquisition of River One, an institutional asset-backed financing platform developing technology to connect stablecoin capital with traditional lending markets. Terms were not disclosed.
Securitize sees an opportunity to modernize the $9 trillion market for asset backed finance by using stablecoins to finance real world assets, generate yield and tokenize investment positions and credit products, Domingo said.
The acquisition also marks an expansion beyond Securitize's core niche markets at a time when tokenization's competitive landscape is growing, with traditional asset managers like BlackRock and Franklin Templeton, and established financial market infrastructure providers like DTCC and Broadridge, entering the industry.
"We have been very active in tokenized funds, treasuries [and] yield … And we've been obviously recently very active in tokenized stocks, so this adds another piece of the puzzle in the emerging tokenization space for us to capture revenue growth."

articles.title: Lucid misses Wall Street’s earnings expectations, expands loan from Saudi Arabia fund
articles.text:
Lucid Group missed Wall Street's third-quarter expectations as the embattled electric vehicle maker continues an "operational reset" aimed at cutting costs and narrowing losses.
The company on Monday also announced a $1.75 billion increase in a delayed draw term loan from Saudi Arabia's Public Investment Fund, the company's largest shareholder.
Lucid stock fell roughly 5% in aftermarket trading Monday.
Here's how Lucid performed in the third quarter compared with average estimates compiled by LSEG:
- Loss per share: $2.74 vs. a loss of $2.28 expected
- Revenue: $350 million vs. $407 million expected
Despite the top- and bottom-line misses, the company's adjusted earnings before interest, taxes, depreciation and amortization of a loss of $726 million beat Wall Street's expectations of a loss of $611 million for the third quarter. Its net loss for the quarter was $830.9 million, down from a loss of $978.4 million a year earlier.
Lucid's 2025 third quarter included revenue of $336.6 million, a loss of $3.31 per share and an adjusted EBITDA loss of $717.7 million.
The quarterly results are the first since Lucid CEO Silvio Napoli, who started leading the company in June, announced a restructuring plan that included implementing several cost-cutting efforts and delaying the company's upcoming midsize vehicle from the end of this year until the second half of next.
"Our transformation is beginning to show progress. We are acting with urgency, strengthening the fundamentals and driving greater discipline, while continuing to invest in the priorities to deliver profitable long-term growth," Napoli said in a release.
The company's turnaround plan includes $1.4 billion in cash flow improvements this year as well as focusing attention on a robotaxi program with Uber and Nuro, a factory that's under construction in Saudi Arabia and the midsize vehicle.
Lucid said the capital from PIF is expected to give the company "additional financial flexibility as Lucid delivers on its turnaround program." It is expected to assist in funding "operations and key investments" into the fourth quarter of 2027, including the start of production for the midsize vehicle.
The additional funds boost Lucid's total liquidity to $3.75 billion, up from $2 billion to end the third quarter.
"We are grateful for the continued financial support from our anchor shareholder, which further energizes us to remain focused on execution and on our commitments as we build a stronger, sustainable Lucid," Napoli said.
Lucid said Monday that the company expects to communicate its midterm plan and targets early next year. The EV maker in May suspended its guidance and many targets, citing new leadership and time needed to develop a turnaround plan.

articles.title: A key report for where inflation stood in October comes out Tuesday. Here's what to expect
articles.text:
Falling gasoline prices provided some relief to consumers in October, but Federal Reserve officials are increasingly concerned that inflation pressures elsewhere in the economy are proving harder to contain.
Prices at the pump declined by more than 4%, according to the Energy Information Administration, providing a respite from a surge that had added more than a dollar a gallon over the past year.
However, the consumer price index for the month, which the Bureau of Labor Statistics will release Tuesday at 8:30 a.m., is expected to show only a slight let-up.
Meanwhile, Fed officials say they are worried that inflation initially driven higher by President Donald Trump's tariffs and the Iran war is proving more persistent than expected, with price pressures emerging in sectors beyond those directly affected by the shocks.
At a time when the central bank is increasingly confident about the state of the labor market, concerns over the cost of living are what are top of mind for the Fed.
"We've been moving up to what historically we'd consider full employment, and the big problem has all been on the inflation side. We go around, we talk to people everywhere in this district, all we hear about is affordability on the business side, the cost," Chicago Fed President Austan Goolsbee said Monday during an event in his home district. "So we've got to come to terms with this cost-side and inflation-side failure."
The CPI reading for all items is expected to show an increase of 0.3%. Core inflation, which excludes volatile food and energy costs, is forecast to increase 0.2%, according to the Dow Jones consensus forecast. While both would be slower than the respective September monthly gains of 0.6% and 0.3%, they still represent further price pressures.
There will be no annual reading for October because of the government shutdown a year ago, which prevented the BLS from collecting some data and compiling a full index level. Because of the data issue, there isn't a comparable figure for the index.
Bank of America, using an assumed baseline interpolating data for the period last year, estimated the annual growth rates at 3.8% for headline and 2.7% for core, both 0.1 percentage point higher than September and well above the Fed's 2% goal.
Goolsbee said the current run on inflation is defying what normally could be expected from supply shocks and tariffs, with the current situation intensified by the hyperscaler build-out related to artificial intelligence.
"It was supposed to have gone away by now, and we're now starting to see the inflation kicking up in areas that probably weren't from oil prices and tariffs, like a bunch of services. Now this stuff with the AI data center build-out is, to my eyes, starting to look more just like old-fashioned demand overheating," he said.
The massive investment in data centers is creating demand for construction workers, electricity and equipment, potentially adding to price pressures even as AI promises longer-term productivity gains, he added.
Pressure on rates
Though the Fed in October voted to hold its benchmark interest rate in place, markets are pricing in a better than 80% probability that the central bank will raise rates by a quarter percentage point at its next meeting in December, according to CME FedWatch data.
Goolsbee, who doesn't vote on the rate-setting Federal Open Market Committee this year but will in 2027, didn't commit to which way he was leaning on additional rate hikes, though he said current conditions could warrant action.
"The conventional wisdom there is: Be aggressive up front, to never let the economy overheat, because once it gets overheated, it's extremely painful to get rid of that kind of overheating," he said. "So I think we've got to watch out in that space."
The CPI release comes with economic growth strong — 3.4% in the third quarter for gross domestic product and tracking at 3.5% for the final three months of the year, according to the Atlanta Fed — and the labor market seemingly in solid shape as well. Nonfarm payrolls expanded by a much better-than-expected 165,000 in October, while the unemployment rate edged lower to 4.1%, though inflation-adjusted wage growth has been negative.
That puts the inflation reading squarely in focus.
Bank of America said it sees tariff impacts fading but that goods prices could be pushed higher because of AI demand. Further, the firm is cautious about "sticky" services prices as well as pressures from health insurance and autos.
The bank has been hawkish in terms of Fed expectations and sees a December hike as likely so long as there isn't an escalated stock market sell-off that might dissuade the central bank.
"This will be the final inflation report before the Fed's December 8-9 meeting. If our forecast is correct, we think it would effectively lock in another 25bp hike, all else equal," BofA economist Stephen Juneau said in a client note. "Absent an indisputably soft 0.1% [month-over-month] print, we doubt the inflation data will dissuade the Fed from hiking in December. The bigger risk to our call comes from financial markets."

articles.title: Children’s Place files for bankruptcy protection, seeks buyer
articles.text:
Children's clothing retailer The Children's Place has filed for chapter 11 bankruptcy protection, it said Sunday.
The company is looking to sell substantially all of its assets and is seeking offers from potential buyers by Dec. 9, with a goal to close a deal by the end of December.
The retailer, whose brands include The Children's Place and Gymboree, says it operates two digital storefronts and 514 North American stores, and has distribution in 13 countries through franchise and wholesale partners. The company's performance has taken a hit in recent years from tariff hikes and slower consumer spending, among other factors.
Its stores and e-commerce sites remain open for now, and the company is planning to continue its ongoing inventory sales with court approval.
"For nearly 60 years, The Children's Place has supported growing families with apparel that customers have come to know and love. We recognize the significance of this development for our employees, customers, vendors, and other partners, and we are committed to conducting an efficient and transparent sale process," said Rudy Morando, co-chief restructuring officer of The Children's Place. "In the meantime, we remain focused on serving the families who have trusted The Children's Place for generations."
This move comes days after interim Children's Place CEO Muhammad Asif Seemab and Chief Strategy Officer Muhammad Umair stepped down from their roles. Seemab and Umair will both remain on the company's board. CFO John Szczepanski took on the role of acting president and principal executive officer.
Seemab is also managing director of Saudi-based Mithaq Capital, which took a majority stake in The Children's Place in 2024 when the company was facing financial trouble.
Even with support from the investors, the company has not been able to significantly improve its financial outlook. In its bankruptcy filing, the company reported about $742 million in assets, compared to about $881 million in debts.
In the second fiscal quarter of 2026, its most recently reported quarter, the company's net sales dropped nearly 19% from the same period the year prior. At the time, Seemab said in a news release that during the quarter the company was "stabilizing our customer file" and "driving traffic to our stores and websites," and saw "lower conversion, combined with a very clearance-heavy mix."
He also pointed to tough comparisons to the prior-year period, due in part to back-to-school shopping demand that "was uniquely elevated ... ahead of anticipated tariff price increases."
The Children's Place stock has plummeted in recent years and was trading around 18 cents per share on Monday.

articles.title: Nvidia’s Trump ties draw scrutiny after reports Huang was targeted by Chinese intelligence
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang has spent the past two years cultivating an unparalleled relationship with President Donald Trump, gaining extraordinary access and influence over federal artificial intelligence policy as his company has pushed for looser restrictions on selling advanced chips to China.
Now, revelations about Huang's affair with a suspected Chinese spy are putting that carefully built alliance under scrutiny — along with the millions of dollars Huang and other Nvidia executives have spent expanding the company's political influence in Washington.
The chipmaker is nearly inseparable from its co-founder and CEO Huang, who during Trump's second term has gone from being nearly unknown to the president to being part of a small cadre of executives accompanying him on Air Force One.
Nvidia has committed at least $26 million to Trump's pet projects, including $25 million toward his White House ballroom and $1 million to his 2025 inaugural fund. The company initially sought to keep its ballroom contribution anonymous, according to documents obtained by The Washington Post. Its ballroom pledge was tied with Apple's for the largest disclosed corporate contribution, the Post reported.
Those ties are drawing renewed scrutiny from congressional Democrats, including Sen. Richard Blumenthal, D-Conn., who pressed Huang in November 2025 about Nvidia's ballroom donation and White House contacts. Blumenthal re-upped his warning on Thursday, while expected incoming House oversight Chairman Robert Garcia, D-Calif., vowed to investigate corporate corruption when Democrats take control in January.
Trump continued to defend Huang on Sunday, calling him an "honorable guy" and saying he had heard nothing suggesting wrongdoing. The president was briefed about the suspected Chinese intelligence operation in October 2025 but chose not to act, according to The New York Times. Secretary of State Marco Rubio oversaw a classified memo detailing the concerns this spring, the Times reported.
The president's defense underscores how Huang has become one of Trump's most prominent allies in the technology industry, repeatedly praising the president, attending White House events and accompanying him on a trip to China in May. Trump is due to return to China next week for a summit with other world leaders.
Congressional scrutiny on Huang ramped up after the Times reported Oct. 29 that U.S. intelligence determined Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen who is an executive at Singapore-based cloud computing company Megaspeed, was funneling information to Beijing and had “developed a close relationship” with Jensen Huang. The two Huangs are unrelated.
House Republican committee leaders on Thursday asked Jensen Huang to sit for a closed-door briefing on his ties with Alice Huang, saying recent reports "raise significant national security concerns regarding the PRC's access to sensitive U.S. technology and information."
In a statement to his company on Sunday, Jensen Huang admitted to the affair and apologized. He also revealed that Nvidia's board of directors has "initiated an independent investigation," which he said he supports and will cooperate with.
"I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting NVIDIA and supporting America's national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American," the CEO said.
Nvidia didn't immediately respond to CNBC's request for comment.
House Minority Leader Hakeem Jeffries, D-N.Y., told CBS News on Monday morning that "high-level" Trump administration officials would lead a classified briefing for lawmakers later in the day. An administration official, speaking on condition of anonymity to discuss the private meeting, told CNBC U.S. intelligence chiefs John Ratcliffe and Jay Clayton were previously scheduled to lead a classified briefing on threats related to Iran with top congressional leaders.
Later Monday morning, the Times reported that the Commerce Department was investigating Megaspeed until August 2025, when the probe was abruptly transferred to the Department of Justice following outreach from Nvidia's general counsel about the matter.
Thomas Wackman, spokesman for Commerce's Bureau of Industry and Security, told CNBC in a statement, "BIS conducts all enforcement strictly by the book. BIS enforces aggressively across the board, including with respect to chip smuggling, and enforcement is at an all-time high." 
The DOJ did not respond to CNBC's request for comment.
"NVIDIA's CEO just confirmed a relationship with a suspected Chinese spy," Sen. Elizabeth Warren, D-Mass., the top Democrat on the Senate Banking Committee who is expected to chair the panel next year, posted on X Monday morning. "Congress is back today. We have legislation ready to go to stop advanced AI chips from fueling China's military."
Huang's access to Trump has coincided with a series of policy reversals that eased restrictions on Nvidia's chip sales to China, a lucrative market the company has fought to preserve.
In April 2025, Huang attended a $1 million-per-person dinner at Mar-a-Lago, after which the administration briefly held off on restricting Nvidia's H20 chips before imposing the limits days later. Following another meeting with Trump in July, the administration reversed course and began approving sales to China.
In December 2025, days after another meeting with Huang, Trump announced plans to permit exports of Nvidia's more powerful H200 chips to approved Chinese customers. The Commerce Department formally relaxed its licensing restrictions the following month.
Huang kept up the pressure in 2026, accompanying Trump on a trip to China as Nvidia fought congressional efforts to tighten export controls.
But Nvidia's success in Washington has yet to translate into unfettered access to China. Beijing has withheld approval for large-scale H200 imports, leaving hundreds of thousands of chips awaiting shipment as of early November.
Nvidia has also quietly ramped up its Washington influence operation, spending a record $2.15 million on federal lobbying in the third quarter — up 72% from the previous quarter and 10% from a year earlier, according to company disclosures. Its $4.69 million in 2026 lobbying expenses through September nearly matches the $4.97 million it spent in all of 2025.
The company's in-house lobbyists include alumni of congressional offices from key Republicans and Democrats, including Rep. Michael McCaul, R-Texas, who previously chaired the House Foreign Affairs Committee.
In June, Nvidia hired former Obama Commerce Department official and Intel lobbying chief Bruce Andrews to lead its Washington operation, then launched its first employee-funded PAC in August. The PAC raised more than $263,000 through September but had yet to back any candidates, according to a CNBC analysis of Federal Election Commission filings. Its next disclosure is due Dec. 3. Separately, two Nvidia executives — Gavin Sherry, vice president of software, and Sundeep Madra, vice president of hardware — each contributed $443,000 to the Republican National Committee on June 24.
The donations help illustrate the depth of Huang and Trump's relationship as the $4.3 trillion tech behemoth Nvidia buoys the U.S. economy and lends crucial advantage over China in the race for AI dominance.
They also raise further questions about the Trump administration's response to U.S. intelligence reportedly revealing that the loyal and powerful Nvidia CEO had a close relationship with a Chinese spy.
"Obviously Nvidia needs to take significant steps in its operations, security, and policy advocacy to ensure it takes national security concerns more seriously," Chris McGuire, a senior fellow for China and emerging technologies at the Council on Foreign Relations, said in an X post Monday. "But it is even more important that the Department of Commerce tighten up export controls to prevent things like this from ever happening again.
"It is utterly baffling that despite being privy to this information for months, they have not taken even the most basic actions to protect the country, such as cutting off a company that is literally run by Chinese spies from buying AI chips," McGuire wrote.

articles.title: PepsiCo to cut about 1,000 jobs as North American business struggles
articles.text:
PepsiCo is cutting about 1,000 jobs across North America as the company tries to turn around lagging sales in its home market.
"We have a clear ambition for PepsiCo North America: to build a stronger, more future-fit business that delivers industry-leading growth," Ram Krishnan, CEO of PepsiCo North America, wrote in a Monday letter to employees obtained by CNBC. "To do that, we need to be faster, more connected, and more capable, while continuing to invest in growth — behind our people, capabilities and brands."
Over the next week, Pepsi plans to cut jobs as it says it aims to streamline its operations and better connect teams across the company's North American business. PepsiCo employs about 306,000 people worldwide, including roughly 125,000 in the United States, as of Dec. 27, according to a company filing.
The Wall Street Journal first reported the coming layoffs.
In October, PepsiCo cut its full-year earnings outlook, citing the struggles in its home market. During the third quarter, its North American beverage unit saw volume shrink 2%, while its North American food division reported flat volume.
While the company has tried to boost sales by cutting prices and investing in marketing, the turnaround is taking longer than expected, Chief Financial Officer Steve Schmitt said on the company's earnings conference call.
Shares of Pepsi rose slightly in afternoon trading. The stock is down nearly 1% this year, lagging behind the S&P 500's gains of nearly 11% over the same period.

articles.title: As Nvidia probes Jensen Huang affair, here's the board member likely to play a big role
articles.text:
Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang is facing an internal investigation after admitting to an affair with a Chinese businesswoman who U.S. intelligence agencies believe is a Chinese spy.
While the company has not yet named specific investigators, that probe is being helmed by the board with help from outside counsel, according to Nvidia. Lawyer Stephen Neal is the board's lead independent director and head of corporate governance, likely making him a key figure in the investigation.
In a statement, Nvidia's board said it has "no reason to believe that either national security or Nvidia secrets were compromised," though it will examine all evidence. China has dismissed the espionage claims. Huang, one of the most powerful businessmen in the artificial intelligence boom, said he would "cooperate fully" with the process.
Yet the probe has sparked uncertainty around Huang's future at the chipmaker and raised concerns of broader ripple effects to companies in the tech sector that are exposed to the AI build-out.
In a Monday note, Citi analysts wrote that one of the key issues for investors moving forward will be "potential governance implications" and "increased regulatory scrutiny" as the company navigates the investigation.
Leading the probe
Nvidia's board has 10 independent members, including a former president of Taco Bell, a former Eli Lilly executive and a former vice chairman from Goldman Sachs. Neal, who joined Nvidia's board of directors in 2019, is a chairman emeritus and senior counsel of the law firm Cooley LLP, where he also served as CEO from 2001 to 2008.
Neal did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
It won't be his first corporate governance probe. According to Cooley, Neal has litigated cases across securities, bankruptcies, antitrust, takeovers and more. And he's conducted several investigations for multiple boards of directors, including at General Motors, where he advised the company in disputes with Ross Perot.
He also guided Walter Hewlett and the Hewlett Trust to stop a merger between Hewlett-Packard Co. and Compaq Computer Corp. and helped PacifiCare Health Systems with transactional matters.
According to the firm, Neal has conducted several investigations for committees of directors and independent directors, though most of those client names are confidential. He's also handled investigations with the Securities and Exchange Commission for both corporations and individuals.
When he joined Nvidia, Neal was also the chairman of the board of directors at Levi Strauss & Co. He stepped down in 2021 after reaching the mandatory board retirement age of 72, the company said at the time. The retailer did not immediately respond to a request for comment from CNBC on Monday.
Cooley has a long history with Nvidia, too. The law firm said it incorporated the company in 1993 and has served as its principal outside corporate and litigation counsel for roughly three decades. Cooley handled Nvidia's initial public offering in 1999.
Investors will be closely watching the investigation, and its emphasis on independence, as the process unfolds, according to Brayden King, a professor of management and organizations at Northwestern University's Kellogg School of Management.
"You definitely want somebody leading it who people can look at and say, 'OK, we believe this is a report that we can fully believe and trust that the outcome is the right outcome,'" King told CNBC. "That's what investors are looking for. They just don't like the instability that comes with all of this."
Looking to corporate governance
King said the Nvidia investigation lies at a unique intersection of Wall Street and Washington, D.C., where the company is likely navigating its next steps to try to appease both groups.
Because Nvidia's reputation is highly correlated with Huang's reputation, King said, conducting a transparent investigation will be key to regaining and retaining shareholders' trust. Not having an immediate CEO succession plan in place is only impeding that confidence, he added.
"I think the board realizes that they're doing an independent investigation in part because they really need to understand to what extent there are real problems here, and they also know that if they don't do an independent investigation, then there will be lingering concerns about whether their key stakeholders can trust the company," King said.
If the investigation shows that national security was indeed put at risk, King said, the company will need to take "very strong measures" to restore its reputation.
"That will basically come down to having to put structures in place in corporate governance to assure that this can't happen again," King said. "The independent review is going to have to be truly independent, and it's going to have to be candid enough that people believe that we can restore some normalcy around how the company operates."
It's also likely influencing how other tech companies, particularly those in the AI space, are thinking about their own corporate governance structures and how they might navigate increased scrutiny on their leaders, he added.
Broader implications
Marcel Kahan, a professor of law at New York University, said he's not surprised that Nvidia has been potentially exposed to industrial espionage.
Because the company operates in such a high-visibility and crucial sector, Kahan said companies like Nvidia have to be careful in their operations and whom they trust with their information. The investigation could mean the company may consider adding additional governance committees to ensure this doesn't happen again.
The revelations about its CEO will also likely mean more specialized training from Nvidia and its law firms to ensure trade secrets are kept close.
He also said the company is likely prioritizing an in-depth investigation over transparency to investors, focusing on recruiting "the best of the best" to assist with the probe.
"Nvidia is one of the most valuable companies on Wall Street," Kahan told CNBC. "I think, given all the attention that's being paid to it, this is one of the instances where I would not be that worried about anything being done in an underhanded way."
Still, although Nvidia is a major company with massive influence on the market, the controversy may not end up making too large of a dent in corporate governance structures, according to Kathryn Harrigan, a professor of business leadership at Columbia Business School.
Harrigan said because Wall Street and Silicon Valley have seen similar controversies play out before, this scandal may simply be following the script of its predecessors.
"Is it going to change the basic structure of the AI build-out? Probably not," she told CNBC. "You sometimes wait years to get on their schedule if you have an order for chips. It's not like you can magically switch from one vendor to another."

articles.title: Không phải Campuchia, đây mới là quốc gia nhận đầu tư nhiều nhất từ Việt Nam, cái tên "lạ" đứng ở vị trí thứ 2
articles.text:
Không phải Campuchia, đây mới là quốc gia nhận đầu tư nhiều nhất từ Việt Nam, cái tên "lạ" đứng ở vị trí thứ 2
Trong 10 tháng đầu năm 2026, có 37 quốc gia và vùng lãnh thổ nhận đầu tư của Việt Nam.
- 10-11-2026Phát hiện nam thanh niên nghỉ hưu ở tuổi 30, thu nhập hàng năm lên tới hơn 800 triệu đồng
- 09-11-2026Tuyên bố không còn phải mua một xu khí đốt nào từ Nga nữa, một nước châu Âu hân hoan đón tin vui
- 08-11-20263 tàu chở 140.000 tấn dầu Nga bất ngờ đổi hướng khi đang trên đường tới Mỹ, Moscow nói gì?
Tổng vốn đầu tư của Việt Nam ra nước ngoài (vốn cấp mới và điều chỉnh) 10 tháng năm 2026 đạt 3,41 tỷ USD, gấp 3,1 lần so với cùng kỳ năm trước, theo Cục Đầu tư nước ngoài (Bộ Tài chính).
Trong 10 tháng đầu năm 2026, có 37 quốc gia và vùng lãnh thổ nhận đầu tư của Việt Nam.
Trong đó, Lào là nước dẫn đầu với 670,9 triệu USD, chiếm 19,7% tổng vốn đầu tư; Cộng hòa Dominica ghi nhận 560 triệu USD (16,4%); Campuchia đạt 487,0 triệu USD (14,3%); Ấn Độ đạt 361,7 triệu USD (10,6%); Indonesia đạt 340,2 triệu USD (10%); Philippines ghi nhận 193,6 triệu USD (5,7%); Kazakhstan đạt 149,9 triệu USD (4,4%); Mỹ gần 100 triệu USD (2,9%). Đáng chú ý, vốn đầu tư vào Dominica đến hoàn toàn từ dự án của Viettel Global.
Hợp tác kinh tế giữa Việt Nam và Lào tiếp tục có những chuyển biến tích cực qua các năm. Năm 2025, kim ngạch thương mại hai chiều đạt khoảng 3 tỷ USD, tăng 32% so với năm 2024. Việt Nam tiếp tục nằm trong nhóm các nhà đầu tư nước ngoài lớn tại Lào, với khoảng 300 dự án, tổng vốn đăng ký khoảng 7,04 tỷ USD tính đến đầu tháng 10.
Những doanh nghiệp tên tuổi như Viettel, Hoàng Anh Gia Lai, Vinamilk, BIDV, Cao su Việt Nam, Petrolimex... đều đang có những khoản đầu tư lớn tại Lào.
Việt Nam hàng ngày

articles.title: Nvidia's China revenue exposure: What New Street estimates
articles.text: Concerns about a potential crackdown on Nvidia's business operations are percolating on Wall Street following revelations about CEO Jensen Huang's involvement with a suspected Chinese spy. As much as 10% of Nvidia's revenues may come directly or indirectly from China, according to a Monday analysis from New Street Research. That amounts to between $37 and $47 billion out of Nvidia's total expected fiscal year 2027 revenue of $411 billion, according to consensus estimates cited by New Street. Of Nvidia's China-exposed revenues, New Street classifies 6% as "legal sales" into China and Hong Kong, and 4% as booked outside of China. Of the latter 4%, the firm estimates that half of it gets physically diverted into China while the other half is used by "Chinese-controlled offshore capacity." Nvidia stock is down about 5% in regular trading on Monday. The U.S. maintains export controls on some of Nvidia's most high-tech chips, though Chinese firms have reportedly been able to access Nvidia-powered computing capacity through other countries. "We are committed to compliance with all U.S. laws and work in collaboration with the entire AI ecosystem and US government," the company told investors at its 2026 annual shareholders meeting. The New York Times reported on Monday that the Commerce Department had already been investigating the company where the suspected Chinese spy was a boss before the investigation was transferred to the Justice Department. The transfer happened after the Commerce Department was contacted by Nvidia's general counsel, the Times reported. Nvidia is one of the most important companies in the wide-ranging artificial intelligence buildout that is in the early stages of remaking the U.S., and perhaps the global, economy. The company is mutually invested with numerous other tech companies in various parts of the AI supply chain and has also built financing platforms for its products with top private credit firms .

articles.title: Tổng thống Mỹ Trump nói lý do tạm hoãn tấn công Iran
articles.text:
Tổng thống Mỹ Trump nói lý do tạm hoãn tấn công Iran
Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump. (Ảnh: Reuters)
Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump cho biết, ông dự định tạm hoãn các cuộc tấn công quân sự mới nhắm vào Iran sau khi nhận được lời kêu gọi từ các lãnh đạo trong khu vực, trong đó có Thủ tướng Qatar.
- 10-11-2026Tổng thống Trump: Ukraine sẽ có hình dạng hơi khác sau thỏa thuận hòa bình
- 09-11-2026Đế chế Nvidia rung chuyển, chiếc ghế của 'ông vua' AI Jensen Huang có lung lay?
- 09-11-2026Tổng thống Mỹ Trump rút lại lời đe dọa tấn công Iran?
Trong một cuộc phỏng vấn với Reuters và sau đó là cuộc họp báo ở Nhà Trắng, Tổng thống Trump cho biết hiện tại ông vẫn dự định duy trì lệnh phong tỏa hải quân tại eo biển Hormuz.
“Mỹ đã chuẩn bị đầy đủ với những khí tài tốt nhất, nhưng chúng tôi hy vọng sẽ không có lý do gì để phải sử dụng đến chúng”, ông Trump phát biểu với các phóng viên.
Ông cho biết mình hành động "theo yêu cầu từ các quốc gia láng giềng của Iran” trong khu vực, cụ thể là Qatar, Ả-rập Xê Út, Các Tiểu vương quốc Ả-rập Thống nhất, Bahrain, Kuwait và một số nước khác, những bên không muốn Mỹ thực hiện thêm các cuộc tấn công mới.
Tổng thống Mỹ đưa ra phát biểu trên sau cuộc gặp với Thủ tướng Qatar, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman Al-Thani - một nhân vật trung gian quan trọng với Tehran - trong bối cảnh các nỗ lực chấm dứt xung đột đang được đẩy mạnh sau cuộc bầu cử giữa kỳ tại Mỹ vào tuần trước.
Sau hơn tám tháng kể từ khi xung đột bùng phát, ông Trump cho rằng khả năng tái diễn một cuộc chiến tranh quy mô lớn trong tương lai gần là thấp, nhưng vẫn không chấp nhận kế hoạch đình chiến do phía Iran đề xuất.
Cùng lúc đó, các cuộc tấn công qua lại vẫn tiếp diễn. Theo truyền thông nhà nước Iran, Mỹ đã thực hiện các đợt không kích vào đảo Qeshm của Iran. Đáp lại, Iran đã tấn công các tàu chở dầu tại vùng Vịnh và eo biển Hormuz, còn lực lượng Houthi ở Yemen - đồng minh của Iran - cũng đã thực hiện các cuộc tấn công nhắm vào Ả-rập Xê-út.
Nỗ lực ngoại giao
Ông Al-Thani, người đồng thời giữ cương vị Thủ tướng và Bộ trưởng Ngoại giao Qatar, đã gặp ông Trump sau khi có chuyến thăm Tehran vào tuần trước.
Vị Thủ tướng cho biết các cuộc thảo luận của ông với ông Trump và Phó Tổng thống JD Vance đều diễn ra tốt đẹp.
"Tôi rất cảm kích trước những cuộc thảo luận tích cực về việc đạt được một thỏa thuận và mang lại hòa bình cho khu vực”, ông chia sẻ trên nền tảng X.
Trong khi đó, ông Mohsen Rezaei - người đứng đầu Hội đồng An ninh Iran - tuyên bố Mỹ nên "ngừng bịa đặt tin giả về các cuộc đàm phán không có thật" và đã đến lúc "chấp nhận bảy điều kiện mà Iran đã nhiều lần đưa ra".
Đề xuất của Iran nhằm chấm dứt chiến tranh bao gồm việc Mỹ dỡ bỏ phong tỏa các cảng biển của Iran, gỡ bỏ một số lệnh trừng phạt và ngừng ném bom. Đổi lại, Tehran sẽ chấm dứt việc phong tỏa eo biển Hormuz. Sau đó, các bên sẽ tiến hành đàm phán về chương trình hạt nhân và các lệnh trừng phạt khác.
Mỹ đã nhiều lần bác bỏ kế hoạch này. Hôm 8/11, Ngoại trưởng Marco Rubio mô tả các điều kiện mà Tehran đưa ra là "hoàn toàn phi thực tế".
Ngày 9/11, người phát ngôn Bộ Ngoại giao Iran - Esmaeil Baghaei - đã lên tiếng bảo vệ kế hoạch, khẳng định đây là đề xuất hợp lý nhất hiện có.
Các thành viên cấp cao của đảng Cộng hòa tại Mỹ, bao gồm cả Phó Tổng thống JD Vance, cho rằng cuộc chiến liên quan đến Iran chính là nguyên nhân dẫn đến thất bại của đảng này trong các cuộc bầu cử tuần trước. Bất chấp áp lực chính trị trong nước ngày càng tăng đòi chấm dứt xung đột, Ngoại trưởng Mỹ Rubio cho biết ông không tin rằng một bước đột phá ngoại giao sắp xảy ra.
Anwar Gargash - một quan chức cấp cao của Các Tiểu vương quốc Ả-rập Thống nhất (UAE) - cũng bày tỏ quan điểm tương tự, cho rằng một giải pháp chính trị toàn diện giữa Mỹ và Iran là điều khó đạt được.
Ông nói: "Chúng ta nên chuẩn bị tinh thần cho một giai đoạn bất ổn kéo dài, trong đó khó có thể kỳ vọng vào một giải pháp dứt điểm hay một trật tự khu vực ổn định".
Nỗi lo ngại về cuộc chiến đã bao trùm khu vực suốt nhiều tháng qua. Hôm 9/11, Tổng thống Thổ Nhĩ Kỳ Tayyip Erdogan cho biết ông đã nói với Tổng thống Mỹ Donald Trump rằng Ankara không muốn chứng kiến bất kỳ sự leo thang căng thẳng nào mới.
"Chúng tôi luôn nhấn mạnh rằng các vấn đề này hoàn toàn có thể được giải quyết thông qua đối thoại và ngoại giao. Đáng tiếc là tình hình lại đang có chiều hướng xấu đi. Chúng tôi đang nỗ lực hết sức để ngăn chặn điều đó”, ông Erdogan phát biểu với các phóng viên.
Các cuộc tấn công qua lại
Một quan chức cấp tỉnh phát biểu với hãng thông tấn bán chính thức Fars của Iran rằng các cuộc tấn công nhắm vào đảo Qeshm hôm 8/11 không gây ảnh hưởng đến cơ sở hạ tầng hay các dịch vụ thiết yếu.
Một nguồn tin cấp cao của Iran tiết lộ, các cuộc tấn công của Mỹ nhắm vào hệ thống radar của Iran - vốn phục vụ cả mục đích phòng không lẫn dẫn đường cho tàu thuyền - cùng các căn cứ đặt bệ phóng tên lửa và hệ thống rải thủy lôi.
Theo số liệu từ các cơ quan hàng hải quốc tế công bố tuần trước, các vụ tấn công nhằm vào tàu chở dầu tại vùng Vịnh và Eo biển Hormuz đã gia tăng mạnh mẽ kể từ tháng 10, duy trì ở mức cao nhất kể từ khi cuộc xung đột bắt đầu.
Iran cho biết hôm 8/11, rằng một tàu chở dầu đã va phải thủy lôi ở phía đông Eo biển Hormuz.
Một phóng viên đài truyền hình nhà nước Iran ngày 9/11 đưa tin, 11 tàu chở dầu đã bị "vô hiệu hóa" trong vòng 10 ngày qua.
Tiền phong

articles.title: The wait is almost over for this blockbuster video game. I see 35% upside in the stock
articles.text: Your favorite tech contrarian is back ... and today's stock pick is a little outside my usual territory. I typically focus on AI infrastructure companies, but right now I see a compelling opportunity in Take-Two Interactive Software, one of the world's largest video game publishers. The New York-based company is behind blockbuster franchises including Grand Theft Auto, NBA 2K and Red Dead Redemption. Its biggest hit, Grand Theft Auto V, has sold more than 230 million copies worldwide, making it one of the best-selling video games of all time. Key points The long-awaited release of Grand Theft Auto VI could drive a major jump in sales and earnings. Wall Street is underestimating how many copies of the game Take-Two could sell. Shares trade at a discount to the industry's historical valuation despite a major growth catalyst on the horizon. The big catalyst for Take-Two is just around the corner: Grand Theft Auto VI is scheduled for release on Nov. 19 . It's been 13 years since the last installment, and several delays have only added to the anticipation. I believe investors are underestimating just how much demand there is for this game, and I see significant upside for the stock over the next couple of years. Grand Theft Auto VI Management has forecast sales of approximately 30 million copies of Grand Theft Auto VI in its first year. We're modeling 37 million, and I think sales could go even higher. Part of the opportunity comes down to management's traditionally conservative approach to guidance. Take-Two tends to set expectations it believes it can meet or exceed, rather than make overly ambitious promises. That caution has contributed to Wall Street underestimating the game's sales potential. Earnings growth could accelerate sharply The company generated approximately $6.7 billion in revenue in fiscal 2026 , which ended March 31. Revenue is expected to rise to roughly $8.5 billion in fiscal 2027, an increase of about 27%. But the real payoff could come the following year. Earnings per share are projected to jump from $6.97 in fiscal 2027 to $10.32 in fiscal 2028. That's an increase of nearly 50%. As Grand Theft Auto VI sales build, Take-Two could see a substantial improvement in profitability. If demand exceeds expectations, as I believe it will, earnings could climb even higher. The stock looks undervalued Despite the excitement surrounding Grand Theft Auto VI, Take-Two isn't trading at the premium valuation you might expect. TTWO YTD mountain Take-Two Interactive Software, Inc., YTD Shares trade at approximately 21 times projected fiscal 2028 adjusted earnings. That leaves room for the stock to climb if Grand Theft Auto VI delivers the growth we're anticipating. I still see an opportunity here. Investors are getting exposure to one of the biggest potential video game launches in history, and I believe the market has yet to fully appreciate the earnings growth it could generate. Why now? With shares recently trading around $212 our two-year price target of $293 implies approximately 35%-40% upside. This is an attractive opportunity to buy the stock before the full impact of Grand Theft Auto VI becomes clear. Bottom line The biggest risk is that Grand Theft Auto VI doesn't live up to expectations. Another delay or disappointing sales could hurt Take-Two's earnings outlook and put pressure on the stock. As I said, Take-Two is a different kind of play for me, but sometimes the best opportunities are outside your typical investing playbook. With a blockbuster launch approaching and shares trading at a discount, I see a path toward our $293 price target over the next two years. articles.title: Kinh nghiệm 12 năm thuê nhà của cô gái SN 1996 ở TP.HCM: Chung cư mới chưa chắc đã tốt hơn chung cư cũ
articles.text:
Kinh nghiệm 12 năm thuê nhà của cô gái SN 1996 ở TP.HCM: Chung cư mới chưa chắc đã tốt hơn chung cư cũ
Vấn đề không chỉ là chuyện tiền nhà hàng tháng đắt hay rẻ.
Đi tìm nhà để thuê và ở dài hạn, chắc hẳn không ít người sẽ nghĩ thế này: Nếu có điều kiện, thuê chung cư là tốt nhất, sinh hoạt trên 1 mặt sàn vừa dễ dọn dẹp, vừa tiện; an ninh và một môi trường sống cũng an toàn hơn, chưa kể nếu chọn tầng cao thì còn có view đẹp. Thế nên cũng không có gì quá khó hiểu khi nhiều người mặc định thuê chung cư mới sẽ có không gian sống tốt hơn chung cư cũ đã có tuổi đời vài chục năm.
Tuy nhiên thực tế không phải lúc nào cũng vậy. Là người có kinh nghiệm thuê chung cư tầm trung với mức giá 13 triệu/tháng, và giờ chuyển sang thuê chung cư cũ với giá rẻ hơn gần 1 nửa, Thanh Trúc - Cô gái SN 1996 ở TP.HCM phải thừa nhận: Mặc định chung cư mới tốt hơn chung cư cũ là một sai lầm.
Vấn đề chưa bao giờ chỉ là chuyện tiền thuê đắt hay rẻ
Trước khi chuyển đến nơi ở hiện tại, Thanh Trúc từng có khoảng 3 năm thuê 1 căn hộ thuộc 1 dự án chung cư cũng mới bàn giao với quy mô 26 tầng, 625 căn. Ở thời điểm đó, số tiền Thanh Trúc phải trả cho căn hộ này là 13 triệu/tháng, chưa bao gồm điện nước, phí quản lý, phí dịch vụ.
Mặc dù bỏ ra số tiền không nhỏ để thuê nhà, nhưng chất lượng cuộc sống và sức khỏe của Thanh Trúc trong 3 năm ở đó lại có phần không được tốt. Cô cho biết căn hộ cũ có trần khá thấp, thiếu gió, nội thất chủ yếu bằng gỗ công nghiệp nên cảm giác khá ngột ngạt. Tường cũng không có khả năng cách âm tốt, khiến cô gặp vấn đề về giấc ngủ suốt thời gian dài.
"Mình ở đó 3 năm thì cả 3 năm mình bị mất ngủ, nhưng lúc đó cũng không nghĩ là do không gian lẫn không khí ở nơi mình sống. Chỉ đến khi chuyển sang căn hộ bây giờ, mình mới nhận ra những điểm trừ của căn chung cư trước đây từng ở".
Tuy nhiên điểm trừ trần thấp và khá bí (Ảnh: NVCC)
Thanh Trúc chia sẻ và cho biết sau khi chuyển ra khỏi căn chung cư 13 triệu/tháng, căn hộ hiện tại mà cô đang thuê có giá 7 triệu/tháng, thuộc một dự án đã bàn giao được hơn 20 năm.
Dù thiết kế căn hộ không hiện đại, tiện ích nội khu cũng không có nhiều như chỗ cũ, nhưng đổi lại, căn hộ này lại giải quyết được mọi bài toán mà trước đây, Thanh Trúc từng không nhận ra: Trần nhà cao, có 2 ban công đối nhau giúp không gian luôn thông thoáng, có gió tự nhiên. Tường căn hộ có khả năng cách âm tốt hơn. Điều khiến Thanh Trúc bất ngờ nhất là dù hai căn hộ chỉ cách nhau khoảng 1km, nhưng cảm giác về chất lượng không khí và không gian sống lại khác biệt rõ rệt.
"Chuyển sang căn hộ này được 1 tuần thì mình tự nhiên hết mất ngủ luôn! Đến chính mình cũng thấy việc này quá vi diệu, và đôi khi cũng tự hỏi là sao trước đây mình không nghĩ đến việc chuyển nhà khi bị mất ngủ dài ngày" - Thanh Trúc kể và cho biết "cơ duyên" khiến cô chuyển nhà chỉ đơn giản là chủ bán nhà, chứ không hẳn là vì muốn giảm ngân sách cho chỗ ở.
Đó cũng là lý do Thanh Trúc cho rằng người thuê nhà không nên mặc định chung cư mới sẽ mang lại chất lượng sống tốt hơn chung cư cũ. Theo cô, điều này chỉ đúng một phần khi xét đến tiện ích nội khu, bởi những chung cư mới thường có nhiều tiện ích hơn, trong khi các công trình cũ có thể không đáp ứng được nhu cầu này.
Tuy nhiên, chất lượng sống không chỉ nằm ở 1 yếu tố đó.
Căn chung cư giá thuê 7 triệu/tháng ở thời điểm Thanh Trúc mới nhận nhà (Ảnh: NVCC)
Thanh Trúc đang trong quá trình sửa sang, chăm chút cho căn hộ mới (Ảnh: NVCC)
"Chung cư mới bàn giao đôi khi không có nhiều chủ sở hữu ở đâu, mà là người ta đầu tư rồi cho thuê lại, nên cũng không thể mặc định cứ chung cư mới là dân trí cao, mà chung cư cũ là dân trí thấp. Như căn cũ mình thuê, dù là dự án mới nhưng ở mấy năm cũng thấy nhiều chuyện "hỡi ơi" lắm, cứ thi thoảng lại có nhà nào đấy ném đồ đạc xuống đất, 12h đêm vẫn hát karaoke, rồi trộm cắp hàng online nữa.
Còn căn chung cư cũ mình đang ở thì hầu hết là các bác đã về hưu, mọi người sống chậm rãi, hành xử đĩnh đạc lắm. Mình dù là người trẻ và đi thuê nhà ở đây, nhưng cũng ở 1 mình và ít khi ồn ào nên lại thấy hợp môi trường sống này hơn. Chắc cũng tùy nhu cầu và tính cách mà mỗi người sẽ có lựa chọn thuê nhà khác nhau, chỉ là đừng mặc định cứ nhà mới, nhà đắt là tốt hơn nhà cũ, nhà rẻ" - Thanh Trúc bộc bạch.
Hiện tại, cô gái SN 1996 này đã có 12 năm kinh nghiệm thuê nhà ở TP.HCM. Nhìn lại không ít lần chuyển nhà, Thanh Trúc cho rằng cho rằng có vài điều quan trọng cần lưu tâm để tìm được căn hộ như ý.
"Đừng vội chốt thuê nhà chỉ vì tiện ích nội khu quá sang xịn mịn, bởi chưa chắc mình đã dùng hết hoặc cần những thứ đó. Thứ cần tập trung và quan tâm là chất lượng căn hộ có có phù hợp với mình hay không.
Đồng thời, mình nghĩ mọi người cũng cần kiểm tra kỹ hiện trạng căn hộ trước khi nhận bàn giao, đọc kỹ hợp đồng về thời hạn báo trước nếu chủ muốn lấy lại nhà, khoản bồi thường khi chấm dứt hợp đồng đột ngột, khả năng chuyển nhượng hợp đồng trong trường hợp bất khả kháng và điều khoản tăng giá thuê" - Thanh Trúc chia sẻ.
Không ngại thừa nhận bản thân đang "nằm thẳng", chưa tính đến chuyện mua nhà
Nhắc đến chuyện mua nhà, Thanh Trúc cho biết đó từng là mục tiêu mà cô theo đuổi khi mới tốt nghiệp Đại học. Ở thời điểm đó, cô gái SN 1996 này cũng từng nghĩ bản thân nên cố gắng mua nhà và tương lai sẽ phải có nhà. Tuy nhiên ở thì hiện tại, chuyện đó lại là thứ mà Thanh Trúc chưa nghĩ đến.
Nói cách khác, cô đang rất tận hưởng việc ở thuê và cũng chẳng tự áp lực với mục tiêu phải đứng tên trong một cuốn sổ đỏ.
Hiện tại, Thanh Trúc hài lòng với việc thuê chung cư ở lâu dài cùng 2 bé mèo (Ảnh: NVCC)
"Mua nhà từng mục tiêu mình nghĩ tới ở thời điểm mới ra trường, đến giờ mình cũng chưa hẳn là từ bỏ mong muốn có nhà. Nhưng mình nghĩ mọi chuyện cũng cần linh hoạt theo điều kiện thực tế của bản thân cũng như tình hình của thị trường.
Với mức lãi suất thả nổi ngân hàng đang cao, mình thấy thuê nhà vẫn là lựa chọn an toàn. Thuê nhà cũng có những điểm trừ, ví dụ điển hình là việc phải tìm nhà, chuyển nhà, mình thấy cũng khá mệt và tốn kém. Nhưng ở thuê thì chỉ mệt lúc đó thôi, cùng lắm là 1-2 tháng, chứ nếu cố vay mua nhà và gánh nợ, mình nghĩ có thể sẽ mệt gần hết cuộc đời mất vì công việc, tài chính cá nhân cũng khó đảm bảo luôn đi lên trong thời gian dài.
Thế nên mình hay nói đùa là mình đang chọn "nằm thẳng", làm việc vừa sức, tận hưởng cuộc sống không có áp lực nợ nần nhiều năm, mình thấy lựa chọn này đủ phù hợp và đủ linh hoạt với mình ở hiện tại" - Thanh Trúc bộc bạch.
Với cô gái SN 1996 này, xác định thuê nhà dài hạn không phải dấu hiệu của việc từ bỏ mục tiêu sở hữu tài sản, chỉ đơn giản là một lựa chọn phù hợp hơn các phương án khác ở thời điểm hiện tại. Khi chưa sẵn sàng về tài chính, việc tận hưởng một không gian sống tốt, duy trì sự thoải mái trong công việc và không phải gánh khoản nợ vượt quá khả năng cũng là cách quản lý cuộc sống có trách nhiệm.
Thanh Niên Việt

articles.title: China Exports YoY
articles.text:
China’s exports increased 35.2% year-on-year to $412.33 billion in October 2026, surpassing market forecasts of 33.5% growth but slightly below September's 36.3% surge. The country's exports continued to benefit from strong demand for chips and AI-related hardware, with exports of integrated circuits soaring 137.1%. Improved US-China relations also provided support after both sides agreed in September to extend the broader trade truce through January, alongside several other trade measures. Exports to the US rose 32.9%, while shipments to the EU increased 24.4%. Exports to ASEAN countries, China’s biggest trading partner by bloc, surged 46.3%. Meanwhile, the EU and China reached a deal last month to cut Chinese hybrid vehicle exports to the bloc by more than half over the coming years, with the restrictions set to take effect on December 1. President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump are expected to hold their third meeting of the year next week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen. source: General Administration of Customs
Exports YoY in China decreased to 35.20 percent in October from 36.30 percent in September of 2026. Exports YoY in China averaged 14.12 percent from 1991 until 2026, reaching an all time high of 154.30 percent in February of 2021 and a record low of -40.60 percent in February of 2020. This page includes a chart with historical data for China Exports YoY. China Exports YoY - data, historical chart, forecasts and calendar of releases - was last updated on November of 2026.

Exports have long been a key driver of China’s rapid economic growth. In recent years, machinery and transport equipment have made up nearly half of all outbound shipments. Within this category, major contributors include electrical machinery and appliances (14%), telecommunications and audio-visual equipment (12%), office and data-processing machines (8%), and industrial machinery and machine parts (5%). Other important export groups include miscellaneous manufactured goods (23%); manufactured products classified by material (16%)—notably textile yarn, fabrics and related articles (5%), metal manufactures (4%), and iron and steel (2%); chemicals and related products (6%); and food and live animals (3%). The European Union and the United States remain China’s largest export markets, each accounting for more than 15% of total shipments. Other significant destinations include Hong Kong, Japan, South Korea, Vietnam, Germany, India, and the Netherlands (around 3% each).

                        China Exports Rise More Than Expected
                    
                    China’s exports increased 35.2% year-on-year to $412.33 billion in October 2026, surpassing market forecasts of 33.5% growth but slightly below September's 36.3% surge. The country's exports continued to benefit from strong demand for chips and AI-related hardware, with exports of integrated circuits soaring 137.1%. Improved US-China relations also provided support after both sides agreed in September to extend the broader trade truce through January, alongside several other trade measures. Exports to the US rose 32.9%, while shipments to the EU increased 24.4%. Exports to ASEAN countries, China’s biggest trading partner by bloc, surged 46.3%. Meanwhile, the EU and China reached a deal last month to cut Chinese hybrid vehicle exports to the bloc by more than half over the coming years, with the restrictions set to take effect on December 1. President Xi Jinping and President Donald Trump are expected to hold their third meeting of the year next week at the APEC summit in Shenzhen.
                    2026-11-10
                    
                        China’s Export Growth Hits Seven-Month High, Beats Forecasts
                    
                    China’s exports surged 36.3% year-on-year to a record $447.18 billion in September 2026, following a 25% increase in August and exceeding expectations of a 25.5% rise. It marked the strongest export growth since February, driven by robust demand for electronics and semiconductors amid a global AI investment boom, alongside a sharp increase in automobile shipments. Exports to the US climbed 39.6% as trade tensions between the two countries eased. Last month, Washington and Beijing announced plans to roll back tariffs on $30 billion worth of goods from each country and extend their broader trade truce by two months, through January. Exports to the EU rose 25.3%, the fastest increase in seven months, while shipments to ASEAN countries soared 52.3%. However, China’s surging exports are drawing growing resistance from its trade partners. On October 9, Beijing and Brussels struck a deal to curb Chinese hybrid vehicle exports to the EU, as the bloc seeks to protect domestic industries.
                    2026-10-14
                    
                        China’s Exports Accelerate on Strong AI-Driven Demand
                    
                    China’s exports surged 25% year-on-year to $401.44 billion in August 2026, following July's 23.9% increase, as the global AI infrastructure buildout continued to drive trade across Asia despite weather-related disruptions to shipping. High-tech products accounted for more than half of export growth, with overseas sales of integrated circuits jumping nearly 130% and high-tech exports rising almost 57%, while vehicle shipments slowed. Exports to the US surged 34.4%, while shipments to the EU rose just 6.6%, the slowest increase in 10 months. Exports to ASEAN countries climbed 30.2%, while shipments to South Korea and Taiwan rose more than 40%. The export boom is deepening tensions with partners concerned that China’s manufacturing dominance is putting pressure on domestic industries. President Xi Jinping is due to meet US President Donald Trump in Washington later this month, while tensions with Brussels are also rising ahead of an October deadline to address trade imbalances.
